content.content:
13:Business associate: (1) Except as provided in paragraph (4) of this definition, business associate means, with respect to a covered entity, a person who:
14-(i) On behalf of such covered entity or of an organized health care arrangement (as defined in this section) in which the covered entity participates, but other than in the capacity of a member of the workforce of such covered entity or arrangement, creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information for a function or activity regulated by this subchapter, including claims processing or administration, data analysis, processing or administration, utilization review, quality assurance, patient safety activities listed at 42 CFR 3.20, billing, benefit management, practice management, and repricing; or
15-(ii) Provides, other than in the capacity of a member of the workforce of such covered entity, legal, actuarial, accounting, consulting, data aggregation (as defined in § 164.501 of this subchapter), management, administrative, accreditation, or financial services to or for such covered entity, or to or for an organized health care arrangement in which the covered entity participates, where the provision of the service involves the disclosure of protected health information from such covered entity or arrangement, or from another business associate of such covered entity or arrangement, to the person.
16-(2) A covered entity may be a business associate of another covered entity.
17-(3) Business associate includes:
18-(i) A Health Information Organization, E-prescribing Gateway, or other person that provides data transmission services with respect to protected health information to a covered entity and that requires access on a routine basis to such protected health information.
19-(ii) A person that offers a personal health record to one or more individuals on behalf of a covered entity.
20-(iii) A subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information on behalf of the business associate.
21-(4) Business associate does not include:
22-(i) A health care provider, with respect to disclosures by a covered entity to the health care provider concerning the treatment of the individual.
23-(ii) A plan sponsor, with respect to disclosures by a group health plan (or by a health insurance issuer or HMO with respect to a group health plan) to the plan sponsor, to the extent that the requirements of § 164.504(f) of this subchapter apply and are met.
24-(iii) A government agency, with respect to determining eligibility for, or enrollment in, a government health plan that provides public benefits and is administered by another government agency, or collecting protected health information for such purposes, to the extent such activities are authorized by law.
25-(iv) A covered entity participating in an organized health care arrangement that performs a function or activity as described by paragraph (1)(i) of this definition for or on behalf of such organized health care arrangement, or that provides a service as described in paragraph (1)(ii) of this definition to or for such organized health care arrangement by virtue of such activities or services.
--
29:Covered entity means:
30-(1) A health plan.
31-(2) A health care clearinghouse.
32-(3) A health care provider who transmits any health information in electronic form in connection with a transaction covered by this subchapter.
33-Disclosure means the release, transfer, provision of access to, or divulging in any manner of information outside the entity holding the information.
34-EIN stands for the employer identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury. The EIN is the taxpayer identifying number of an individual or other entity (whether or not an employer) assigned under one of the following:
35-(1) 26 U.S.C. 6011(b), which is the portion of the Internal Revenue Code dealing with identifying the taxpayer in tax returns and statements, or corresponding provisions of prior law.
36-(2) 26 U.S.C. 6109, which is the portion of the Internal Revenue Code dealing with identifying numbers in tax returns, statements, and other required documents.
37-Electronic media means:
38-(1) Electronic storage material on which data is or may be recorded electronically, including, for example, devices in computers (hard drives) and any removable/transportable digital memory medium, such as magnetic tape or disk, optical disk, or digital memory card;
39-(2) Transmission media used to exchange information already in electronic storage media. Transmission media include, for example, the Internet, extranet or intranet, leased lines, dial-up lines, private networks, and the physical movement of removable/transportable electronic storage media. Certain transmissions, including of paper, via facsimile, and of voice, via telephone, are not considered to be transmissions via electronic media if the information being exchanged did not exist in electronic form immediately before the transmission.
40:Electronic protected health information means information that comes within paragraphs (1)(i) or (1)(ii) of the definition of protected health information as specified in this section.
41-Employer is defined as it is in 26 U.S.C. 3401(d).
42-Family member means, with respect to an individual:
43-(1) A dependent (as such term is defined in 45 CFR 144.103), of the individual; or
44-(2) Any other person who is a first-degree, second-degree, third-degree, or fourth-degree relative of the individual or of a dependent of the individual. Relatives by affinity (such as by marriage or adoption) are treated the same as relatives by consanguinity (that is, relatives who share a common biological ancestor). In determining the degree of the relationship, relatives by less than full consanguinity (such as half-siblings, who share only one parent) are treated the same as relatives by full consanguinity (such as siblings who share both parents).
45-(i) First-degree relatives include parents, spouses, siblings, and children.
46-(ii) Second-degree relatives include grandparents, grandchildren, aunts, uncles, nephews, and nieces.
47-(iii) Third-degree relatives include great-grandparents, great-grandchildren, great aunts, great uncles, and first cousins.
48-(iv) Fourth-degree relatives include great-great grandparents, great-great grandchildren, and children of first cousins.
49-Genetic information means:
50-(1) Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3) of this definition, with respect to an individual, information about:
51-(i) The individual's genetic tests;
52-(ii) The genetic tests of family members of the individual;
--
75:Health information means any information, including genetic information, whether oral or recorded in any form or medium, that:
76-(1) Is created or received by a health care provider, health plan, public health authority, employer, life insurer, school or university, or health care clearinghouse; and
77-(2) Relates to the past, present, or future physical or mental health or condition of an individual; the provision of health care to an individual; or the past, present, or future payment for the provision of health care to an individual.
78-Health insurance issuer (as defined in section 2791(b)(2) of the PHS Act, 42 U.S.C. 300gg-91(b)(2) and used in the definition of health plan in this section) means an insurance company, insurance service, or insurance organization (including an HMO) that is licensed to engage in the business of insurance in a State and is subject to State law that regulates insurance. Such term does not include a group health plan.
79-Health maintenance organization (HMO) (as defined in section 2791(b)(3) of the PHS Act, 42 U.S.C. 300gg-91(b)(3) and used in the definition of health plan in this section) means a federally qualified HMO, an organization recognized as an HMO under State law, or a similar organization regulated for solvency under State law in the same manner and to the same extent as such an HMO.
80:Health plan means an individual or group plan that provides, or pays the cost of, medical care (as defined in section 2791(a)(2) of the PHS Act, 42 U.S.C. 300gg-91(a)(2)).
81-(1) Health plan includes the following, singly or in combination:
82-(i) A group health plan, as defined in this section.
83-(ii) A health insurance issuer, as defined in this section.
84-(iii) An HMO, as defined in this section.
85-(iv) Part A or Part B of the Medicare program under title XVIII of the Act.
86-(v) The Medicaid program under title XIX of the Act, 42 U.S.C. 1396, et seq.
87-(vi) The Voluntary Prescription Drug Benefit Program under Part D of title XVIII of the Act, 42 U.S.C. 1395w-101 through 1395w-152.
88-(vii) An issuer of a Medicare supplemental policy (as defined in section 1882(g)(1) of the Act, 42 U.S.C. 1395ss(g)(1)).
89-(viii) An issuer of a long-term care policy, excluding a nursing home fixed indemnity policy.

Anthropic's official help pages say it signs a BAA for its HIPAA-ready offerings, mainly first-party API and Enterprise plans, but coverage varies by feature and needs setup.

- **Scope:** Anthropic's help center describes a BAA covering its HIPAA-ready services, such as the first-party API or Enterprise plans. Standard Enterprise plans lack BAA coverage until an administrator acts.
- **Feature coverage:** The official table lists many API features as covered, including Token Counting, Models, Compliance, Prompt Caching, Memory, and Web Search. The Batch API is listed as not covered and not accessible for HIPAA-Ready API users. In the consumer-facing table, Claude in Chrome's third-party data flows are not covered.
- **Claude Code and Cowork:** Claude Code CLI via the first-party API console is eligible only with zero data retention enabled. A HIPAA configuration setting extends coverage to Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode).
- **Enablement:** Coverage for Enterprise features requires the Primary Owner to turn on HIPAA compliance in the organization's "Data and privacy" settings.
- **Eligibility:** Anthropic's older FAQ says the BAA is available only to customers who qualify for certain HIPAA-eligible services, such as those under zero data retention agreements, and that configuration requirements and feature limits apply.
- **Authoritative list:** Anthropic points to the Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities on its Trust Center for the contractual list of Eligible Services.

Caveats: The search results conflict in places. For example, one third-party review says Anthropic offers a BAA only for Enterprise and the developer API, and an older FAQ says the BAA may not apply to web search, while the current official table lists Web Search as covered. Third-party sites (Aptible, IntuitionLabs, Chat Data, BastionGPT) are secondary and sometimes dated; the Anthropic help center and Trust Center documents should be treated as controlling. A BAA is necessary but not sufficient for HIPAA compliance, since the surrounding implementation must also meet HIPAA requirements.

The page's definitions are longer than the 125-character quote limit, so each entry below quotes the opening portion verbatim and paraphrases the rest.

**1. FIPS 201-3** (adapted from OMB M-17-12)
> "Information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity—such as name, social security number…"

The rest adds that the information can also identify a person when linked with other linkable details, such as birth details or family-related identifiers.

**2. CNSSI 4009-2022, NIST SP 800-188, NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, NIST SP 800-53A Rev. 5, NIST SP 800-53B** (all from OMB Circular A-130, 2016). **NISTIR 8228** is also listed for this definition.
> "Information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined…"

The rest says the information counts as PII whether it stands alone or is combined with other linked or linkable information.

**3. NIST SP 800-79-2** (under PII from EGovAct)
> "Any representation of information that permits the identity of an individual to whom the information applies…"

The rest says the definition covers any form of data from which a person's identity can be reasonably inferred, whether directly or indirectly.

**4. NIST SP 800-122** (under PII from GAO Report 08-536)
> "Any information about an individual maintained by an agency, including (1) any information that can be used…"

The rest explains that this includes data that can identify a person and any other data linked or linkable to that person, such as medical, educational, financial, or employment records.

**5. NIST SP 800-88r2** (under Personally identifiable information)
> "Any data that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or in combination…"

The rest says the data counts as PII when combined with other information.

**6. NISTIR 8053** (from GAO Report 08-536) and **NIST SP 800-122**
This entry uses the same wording as Definition 4, so the excerpt above applies here as well.

content.content:
**Updated date:** The page says only "Updated over a week ago," with no specific date.

**Products and plans covered**
- The BAA covers "HIPAA-ready services, such as use of our first-party API, Claude in Microsoft Foundry, or Enterprise plans."
- It covers only the single organization that accepted it.
- Covered Enterprise features depend on the BAA version. Some are covered only under versions accepted after 12/2/25.

**Eligibility conditions**
- **Enterprise:** "Standard Claude Enterprise plans do not include BAA coverage without action from a Primary Owner." The Primary Owner must activate HIPAA compliance under "Data and privacy" and accept the BAA.
- **1P API:** "To use the 1P API with PHI, your organization's Primary Owner will need to sign a BAA" and then contact Anthropic or Sales to enable it.
- **HIPAA configuration:** For Claude Code and Cowork (local mode), "the Primary Owner must also apply the HIPAA configuration to both products."
- **Zero data retention (ZDR):** "Covered Models require 30-day data retention." Claude Code can't use Covered Models while ZDR is enabled for Claude Code, unless Anthropic expressly authorizes it.

**Claude Code coverage**
- **Terminal and Code tab (local mode):** Covered with the HIPAA configuration, but only "when members sign in with their Claude Enterprise account and Claude Code connects directly to Anthropic."
- **Console API key:** Covered only with ZDR, "Covered through ZDR, not through the HIPAA configuration."
- **IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains):** Not covered. "The extensions run on a member's computer, but Claude Code (local mode) includes only the terminal and the Code tab."
- **Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry:** Not covered for Claude Code. "Claude Code (local mode) is covered only when Claude Code connects directly to Anthropic." The page does not mention Vertex AI by name.

**Not covered (examples)**
- Claude Code cloud sessions, the mobile app, and Remote Control are not available under the HIPAA configuration.
- Cowork in the cloud and Dispatch are not available under the HIPAA configuration.
- Connectors, local MCP servers, desktop extensions, Claude in Chrome, and skills or plugins are available but not covered.
- Batch API, Files API, Skills API, Code Execution, and Web Fetch are not covered.
- Claude Design, Claude Slides, Claude Docs, and Claude Science (beta) are not covered.
- Claude Console is excluded from the BAA.
- Without the HIPAA configuration, Cowork is not covered.

**Team plan:** The page does not mention the Team plan.

**Trust Center:** The page points to the "Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities" on the Anthropic Trust Center, which it describes as "the contractual list of Eligible Services." It also links a separate implementation guide for the HIPAA-ready offering.

Kết quả tìm kiếm cho thấy khung pháp lý đã thay đổi, và Nghị định 13/2023 không còn là văn bản hiện hành:

- **Luật và thời điểm hiệu lực:** Luật Bảo vệ dữ liệu cá nhân 2025 (Luật số 91/2025/QH15) được Quốc hội thông qua ngày 26/6/2025 và có hiệu lực từ ngày 01/01/2026.
- **Nghị định hướng dẫn mới:** Nghị định 356/2025/NĐ-CP được ban hành ngày 31/12/2025 và có hiệu lực vào ngày 01/01/2026. Nghị định này thay thế Nghị định 13/2023/NĐ-CP.
- **Phân loại dữ liệu nhạy cảm:** Luật vẫn giữ nguyên hệ thống phân loại hai cấp độ từ Nghị định 13. Theo Nghị định 13, các loại dữ liệu nhạy cảm như thông tin thanh toán, tình trạng sức khỏe hay quan điểm chính trị phải được bảo vệ đặc biệt nghiêm ngặt hơn, bao gồm cả việc đánh giá tác động xử lý dữ liệu. Nghị định 356 mở rộng phạm vi và cụ thể hóa rõ ràng hơn các loại dữ liệu cá nhân nhạy cảm so với Nghị định 13.
- **Thông tin tài khoản ngân hàng:** Kết quả tìm kiếm không xác nhận rõ việc số tài khoản ngân hàng được liệt kê cụ thể trong danh mục nhạy cảm của Luật hay Nghị định 356. Bạn nên kiểm tra điều khoản gốc để xác nhận.
- **Nguồn chính thức:** Không có kết quả nào từ vanban.chinhphu.vn, nên tôi không xác minh được nội dung văn bản gốc.
- **Lưu ý về quan hệ giữa các văn bản:** Một bài viết từ tháng 8/2025 cho rằng Luật không trực tiếp bãi bỏ Nghị định 13, nhưng bài viết này cũ hơn Nghị định 356 nên có thể không còn phản ánh tình hình hiện tại.

content.content:
10:- **[Đề]** dữ kiện có trong đề bài (`work/00-challenge.md`), đã đọc trong phiên này ✅.
14:Ký hiệu loại dữ liệu bị ảnh hưởng: **MED** hồ sơ y tế / chẩn đoán / lịch sử claim · **NID** CCCD / national ID ·
15:**BANK** tài khoản ngân hàng · **TEN** cách ly giữa các tenant (insurer partner, nhiều quốc gia).
28:| P1 | "Engineers run Claude Code on their laptops, signed in to AWS through their SSO profiles." | **P1a.** Agent chạy bằng đúng identity của người. Trong log AWS không phân biệt được hành động do người gõ hay do agent tự quyết. | Khi có sự cố, không trả lời được "ai/cái gì đã làm việc này", và cũng không chứng minh được điều đó với auditor. Trách nhiệm giải trình (named person) bị mờ. | MED, NID, BANK |
29:| | | **P1b.** Laptop là môi trường thực thi có quyền cloud. Laptop bị mất, bị malware, hoặc session SSO bị đánh cắp thì kẻ tấn công kế thừa quyền đó. | Một endpoint bị chiếm dẫn tới truy cập cloud. Phạm vi thiệt hại phụ thuộc vào quyền của profile (xem P2). | MED, NID, BANK |
30:| | | **P1c.** Agent đọc nội dung không tin cậy (log, ticket, tài liệu, output tool, trang web) trong khi đang cầm credential cloud. | Prompt injection gián tiếp: nội dung bị cài cắm có thể khiến agent chạy lệnh đọc/ghi/xoá bằng quyền của engineer. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
31:| P2 | "Most engineers' profiles can reach production." | **P2a.** Quyền truy cập prod là thường trực (standing) và rộng, không gắn với một nhiệm vụ hay khoảng thời gian. | Vi phạm least privilege, đây là kiểm soát cốt lõi của ISO 27001 (access control) và HIPAA (minimum necessary). Mọi rủi ro ở P1 nhân lên theo số người có quyền. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
32:| | | **P2b.** "Reach" không phân biệt đọc với ghi, cũng không phân biệt metadata (config, metrics) với dữ liệu (bản ghi DB, file trong S3). | Một phiên debug đơn giản có thể kéo dữ liệu bệnh nhân hoặc CCCD vào context của agent, tức là ra khỏi ranh giới hệ thống của Papaya (xem P12). | MED, NID, BANK |
34:| P3 | "Some engineers run Claude Code with permission prompts turned off because 'it is faster'." | **P3a.** Điểm dừng duy nhất giữa ý định của agent và hành động thật bị tắt. | Lệnh phá huỷ hoặc lệnh do prompt injection gây ra chạy ngay, không ai thấy trước. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
37:| P4 | "Engineers install MCP servers and plugins they find useful; there is no review process." | **P4a.** Rủi ro chuỗi cung ứng: MCP server/plugin là code bên thứ ba chạy trên laptop có credential cloud. | Code độc hoặc bị chiếm quyền có thể đọc credential, thực thi lệnh, gửi dữ liệu ra ngoài. | MED, NID, BANK |
38:| | | **P4b.** MCP server có thể gửi dữ liệu mà agent đọc được tới dịch vụ bên ngoài. | Dữ liệu nhạy cảm đi tới bên xử lý không có hợp đồng (BAA/DPA). Có thể là vi phạm HIPAA hoặc luật dữ liệu khu vực. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
40:| P5 | "Some workflows use a long-lived GitHub token and AWS access keys stored as repository secrets." | **P5a.** AWS access key dài hạn: không tự hết hạn, khó biết ai đang dùng, dễ lộ qua log hoặc fork. | Key bị lộ cho kẻ tấn công quyền deploy hoặc truy cập dữ liệu cho tới khi bị phát hiện và thu hồi thủ công. | MED, NID, BANK |
42:| | | **P5c.** Repository secret dùng chung cho cả monorepo: workflow nào, branch nào cũng có thể chạm tới (xem A6). | Ai sửa được workflow là có thể dùng secret prod, kể cả qua PR chưa được review. Điều này phá vỡ nguyên tắc "named reviewer" của Compliance ngay ở tầng CI. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
44:| P6 | "Monitoring and alerting exist but are fragmented across CloudWatch, GCP, and Slack channels." | **P6a.** Không có một nơi nhìn toàn cảnh. Tín hiệu bất thường (truy cập dữ liệu lạ, hành động agent lạ) dễ bị bỏ sót. | Phát hiện xâm phạm muộn. HIPAA và luật khu vực có thời hạn thông báo vi phạm; phát hiện muộn có thể dẫn tới vi phạm cả thời hạn. | MED, NID, BANK |
46:| P7 | "On-call is informal." | **P7a.** Không có người chịu trách nhiệm rõ ràng khi có sự cố, cũng không có quy trình leo thang. | Sự cố kéo dài. Trong lúc gấp, người ta dùng quyền rộng nhất có trong tay, đúng kiểu hành vi mà Compliance lo. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
50:| P9 | "Claude Code (Team Premium) is the primary tool for writing code, running git, opening PRs" | **P9a.** Phần lớn code, kể cả IaC, do agent viết. Agent có thể đưa secret vào code, thêm dependency không tồn tại hoặc độc (package bịa tên), hoặc viết code có lỗ hổng. **P9b.** Agent tự chạy git và mở PR. Nếu branch protection yếu, agent hoặc tác giả có thể đẩy thẳng lên nhánh deploy. **P9c.** PR do agent tạo dễ dài và nhiều, nên reviewer dễ duyệt cho qua. | Đường PR → CI chính là đường thay đổi prod. Một PR lỗi được duyệt hời hợt vẫn có "named reviewer" trên giấy, nhưng kiểm soát không còn ý nghĩa thật. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
56:| A1 | AWS: Lambda (Serverless), ECS, EC2, Aurora PostgreSQL, SNS, SQS, Step Functions, S3, CloudWatch | Nhiều loại tài nguyên, và mỗi loại có **nhiều đường thay đổi**: Pulumi, `serverless deploy`, AWS CLI/console, thao tác trực tiếp lên DB. | Một quy tắc "mọi thay đổi phải qua duyệt" chỉ có nghĩa khi bao được **mọi** đường. Bỏ sót một đường là có đường vòng. | MED, NID, BANK |
57:| A2 | "S3 (claim documents)" | Hồ sơ claim (chứa MED/NID/BANK) nằm ở S3. Quyền S3 rộng trên prod tương đương quyền đọc toàn bộ hồ sơ. | Rò rỉ hàng loạt. Đây là loại dữ liệu đắt nhất khi bị lộ. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
58:| A3 | Aurora PostgreSQL | Debug DB dễ thành chạy SQL trực tiếp, cả đọc lẫn ghi, trên dữ liệu thật. | Thay đổi dữ liệu không qua review; `SELECT` kéo dữ liệu cá nhân vào context agent. | MED, NID, BANK, TEN |
61:| A6 | Firebase Hosting cho frontend | Deploy frontend dùng credential riêng (Firebase/GCP). | Thêm một loại credential CI cần quản lý. Frontend bị sửa có thể dẫn tới đánh cắp dữ liệu người dùng nhập vào. | NID, BANK |
62:| A7 | AI agents trong prod (claim assessment, document extraction, FWA) "read documents uploaded by partners and members" | **A7a.** Tài liệu do bên ngoài upload là input không tin cậy với agent prod. **A7b.** Khi engineer dùng Claude Code để debug agent prod, coding agent cũng đọc chính những tài liệu đó, trong khi đang cầm quyền cloud. | **A7b là rủi ro đặc thù của Papaya:** một tài liệu claim bị cài cắm có thể thành prompt injection vào coding agent của engineer. ### 1.11 PHI và dữ liệu nhạy cảm: định nghĩa và phạm vi

Accessed 2026-11-08. Sources:

- Regulation text: 45 CFR 160.103, 164.308, 164.314, 164.501, 164.502, 164.504, 164.514. Read on
  eCFR via its official API, as of 2026-11-01 (**local check**: `curl --compressed`, HTTP 200).
- Anthropic: the BAA help article and the [hipaa-setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hipaa-setup)
  page.
- AWS: the HIPAA eligible services reference.
- NIST CSRC glossary.

**Source gap:** the HHS.gov HIPAA pages (Privacy Rule summary, business associates, cloud computing
guidance, de-identification) returned **HTTP 403** to both WebFetch and curl (**local check**). I
could not read them, so every claim below rests on the regulation text that HHS administers. The
HHS links are given for human readers, marked 📖.

#### 1.11.1 Definitions

| # | Finding | Marker | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.11.1.1 | **Health information** is any information, "oral or recorded in any form or medium", that (1) "is created or received by a health care provider, health plan, public health authority, employer, life insurer, school or university, or health care clearinghouse" and (2) "relates to the past, present, or future physical or mental health or condition of an individual; the provision of health care to an individual; or the past, present, or future **payment** for the provision of health care to an individual." | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103) |
| 1.11.1.2 | **Individually identifiable health information** is "a subset of health information, **including demographic information** collected from an individual", that is created or received by a provider, health plan, employer or clearinghouse, relates to health, care or payment as above, **and** "(i) that identifies the individual; or (ii) with respect to which there is a reasonable basis to believe the information can be used to identify the individual." | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103) |
| 1.11.1.3 | **PHI** is "individually identifiable health information" that is transmitted or maintained by electronic media or "in any other form or medium". Four things are excluded: FERPA education records, records described at 20 U.S.C. 1232g(a)(4)(B)(iv), "employment records held by a covered entity in its role as employer", and information about a person "deceased for more than 50 years". **ePHI** is the electronic subset. | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103); HHS summary 📖 [Privacy Rule summary](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/laws-regulations/index.html) (403, not read) |
| 1.11.1.4 | **Covered entity** means "(1) A health plan. (2) A health care clearinghouse. (3) A health care provider who transmits any health information in electronic form in connection with a transaction covered by this subchapter." A health plan includes "a health insurance issuer". | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103); 📖 [HHS covered entities](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/index.html) (403) |
| 1.11.1.5 | A **business associate** is a person who, on behalf of a covered entity, "creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information" for a regulated function, "**including claims processing or administration, data analysis, processing or administration** … billing, benefit management". The term also covers "a subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information on behalf of the business associate." | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103) |
| 1.11.1.6 | **Payment** includes "adjudication or subrogation of health benefit claims", "billing, claims management, collection activities … and related health care data processing", and "review of health care services with respect to medical necessity, coverage under a health plan". | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.501](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.501) |
| 1.11.1.7 | **De-identified** information is not individually identifiable, so it is not PHI. Under the safe-harbor method it counts as de-identified only if 18 identifier types are removed, including names, address parts smaller than a state, dates other than the year, phone and email, "(G) Social security numbers", "(H) Medical record numbers", "(I) Health plan beneficiary numbers", "(J) Account numbers", "(K) Certificate/license numbers", URLs, **IP addresses**, full-face photos, and "(R) Any other unique identifying number, characteristic, or code". The covered entity must also have no "actual knowledge" that the rest could identify the person. (The other method is an expert determination; not read in detail.) | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.514(a)–(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.514); 📖 [HHS de-identification guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/de-identification/index.html) (403) |
| 1.11.1.8 | **Minimum necessary:** when using or disclosing PHI, a covered entity or business associate "must make reasonable efforts to limit protected health information to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose". | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.502(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.502) |
| 1.11.1.9 | **PII** is not a HIPAA term: the seven HIPAA sections downloaded contain no occurrence of "personally identifiable" (**local check**: `grep -c -i`, 0 in each). The US federal definition (OMB Circular A-130, used in NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5) is "information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual". NIST SP 800-122 lists medical, educational, financial and employment information as examples of linked information. | ✅ | [NIST CSRC glossary: PII](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/personally_identifiable_information) |
| 1.11.1.10 | **PHI vs PII (inference from 1.11.1.1–1.11.1.9):** PII is defined by **identifiability alone**. PHI needs **three things together**: identifiable, about health, care or payment for care, and created or received by a covered entity, or held by a business associate on its behalf. So most PHI is PII, but most PII is not PHI. An identifier such as an ID number or a bank account number becomes part of PHI when it sits in the same record as health or claim information held for a covered entity. | ⚠️ inference (no source states this comparison; derived from the definitions above) | — |
| 1.11.1.11 | **Does HIPAA apply to Papaya at all?** HIPAA's definitions refer to US law: a "health insurance issuer" must be "licensed to engage in the business of insurance in a **State**". Papaya serves insurers "across SEA and Asia" (`work/00-challenge.md`). Whether any Papaya tenant is a HIPAA covered entity, and so whether Papaya is a business associate, is a **legal question I cannot answer**. This file follows the brief, which lists HIPAA as a compliance requirement, and treats Papaya as a business associate of its insurer clients: claims processing on their behalf matches 1.11.1.5. | ✅ (definition text) / ⚠️ (applicability: needs Papaya legal) | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103) |
| 1.11.1.12 | **Regional law** (for example Vietnam, implied by "CCCD"): I could not find and read an official government source this session for how local law classifies health data, national ID and bank data. Secondary sources (law-firm and advisory sites) say Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Law (No. 91/2025/QH15) took effect on 2026-01-01, with Decree 356/2025/NĐ-CP replacing Decree 13/2023/NĐ-CP, and that health data and some financial data are "sensitive personal data". **Not verified. Do not use it in `docs/` until it is read in the official text** (Topic 5). | ⚠️ (secondary sources only) | e.g. [EY legal alert, Decree 356/2025](https://www.ey.com/vi_vn/technical/tax/tax-and-law-updates/nghi-dinh-so-356-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-chi-tiet-mot-so-dieu-va-bien-phap-thi-hanh-luat-bao-ve-du-lieu-ca-nhan) (not official) |

#### 1.11.2 Which group each Papaya data type falls into

This applies 1.11.1 to the data the brief names. The legal text is ✅; **applying it to Papaya is
my inference (⚠️)**, because I have not seen Papaya's schemas or contracts. It assumes the HIPAA
framing of 1.11.1.11.

| Data (code from `work/01-problem-framing.md`) | Group | Why (rule) |
|---|---|---|
| Medical records, medical documents (MED) | **PHI** | Relates to "physical or mental health or condition" and identifies the member (1.11.1.1–1.11.1.3) |
| Diagnoses (MED) | **PHI** | Same rule as medical records |
| Claim history (MED) | **PHI**, even without a diagnosis | Claims are "payment for the provision of health care" (1.11.1.1, 1.11.1.6) |
| National ID / CCCD (NID) | **PII** on its own. **Part of PHI** when it is in a member or claim record | An identifying number. Safe harbor lists "(R) any other unique identifying number" (1.11.1.7); "(G) SSN" is the US equivalent |
| Bank account (BANK) | **PII** (financial) on its own. **Part of PHI** when it is the payout account of a claim | "(J) Account numbers" is a listed identifier (1.11.1.7), and claim payout is payment for care (1.11.1.6) |
| Policy and member numbers | **Part of PHI** in claim context | "(I) Health plan beneficiary numbers" (1.11.1.7) |
| Same data, de-identified by safe harbor | **Not PHI** | 1.11.1.7. Under local law it may still be personal data (1.11.1.12, ⚠️) |
| Infrastructure metadata (resource names, metrics, config without customer values) | **Neither** | Provided it carries none of the 18 identifiers. **Caution:** IP addresses, URLs with IDs, and object keys that contain names or ID numbers are identifiers (1.11.1.7) |

**Practical consequence (inference ⚠️):**
- Claim records combine MED with NID and BANK, so any production store or stream that carries claim
  data should be treated as PHI-bearing as a whole: Aurora claim tables, the claim-documents S3
  bucket, and the queues and logs of claim services.
- Separating PII from PHI field by field is not a safe basis for agent access.

#### 1.11.3 Conditions for a model provider (or any vendor) to process PHI

| # | Finding | Marker | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.11.3.1 | A covered entity may let a business associate "create, receive, maintain, or transmit" PHI only after it "obtains satisfactory assurance that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information". A business associate may do the same with a **subcontractor**, after it obtains the same assurances. The assurances "must be documented through a written contract or other written agreement" (the BAA). The Security Rule has the same requirement for ePHI. | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.502(e)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.502), [164.308(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.308), [164.314(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.314) |
| 1.11.3.2 | Required BAA content includes these duties. The vendor must: not use or disclose PHI beyond the contract; "use appropriate safeguards and comply … with subpart C" (Security Rule); report any use or disclosure not provided for, including breaches; flow the same terms down to its subcontractors; and return or destroy PHI at termination "if feasible". | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.504(e)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.504), [164.314(a)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.314) |
| 1.11.3.3 | **Application to Papaya (inference):** if Papaya is a business associate of its insurers (1.11.1.11), any model provider that receives PHI from a Papaya agent is Papaya's **subcontractor**. Papaya then needs a BAA with that provider, and must also check that its own BAAs with insurers allow the subcontracting. | ⚠️ inference from 1.11.3.1 | — |
| 1.11.3.4 | **Anthropic BAA scope:** it covers "HIPAA-ready services, such as use of our first-party API, Claude in Microsoft Foundry, or Enterprise plans". "Standard Claude Enterprise plans do not include BAA coverage without action from a Primary Owner." The authoritative list of Eligible Services is the Implementation Guide on the Anthropic Trust Center (not opened). **The Team plan is not mentioned**, so treat Team as not covered (⚠️, confirm with Anthropic). | ✅ (article) / ⚠️ (Team) | [Anthropic: BAA for commercial customers](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/8114513-business-associate-agreements-baa-for-commercial-customers) (page shows "Updated over a week ago", no date) |
| 1.11.3.5 | **Claude Code under the Anthropic BAA:** terminal and Code tab (local mode) are covered **with the HIPAA configuration** only "when members sign in with their Claude Enterprise account and Claude Code connects directly to Anthropic". A Console API key is "covered through ZDR, not through the HIPAA configuration". The VS Code and JetBrains extensions are **not** covered. Claude Code through Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS or a Claude apps gateway is **not eligible** for the HIPAA configuration. Connectors, local MCP servers, skills and plugins are available but "not covered". | ✅ | [Anthropic BAA article](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/8114513-business-associate-agreements-baa-for-commercial-customers), [hipaa-setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hipaa-setup) |
| 1.11.3.6 | The HIPAA configuration "doesn't remove cloud provider or GitHub credentials". Data an agent sends to GitHub or another service is **not covered** by the Anthropic BAA. | ✅ | [hipaa-setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hipaa-setup) |
| 1.11.3.7 | **AWS:** Amazon Bedrock, CloudWatch Logs, S3, Aurora and Lambda are on the HIPAA eligible services list. PHI may be used in them only after "entering into an AWS business associate agreement" (page last updated 2026-10-15). Whether Papaya has an AWS BAA is unknown (⚠️). If Claude Code uses Bedrock, the AWS BAA applies to it rather than the Anthropic BAA; I have **not** verified how far that coverage extends to Claude Code (⚠️). | ✅ (list) / ⚠️ (Papaya status, Claude Code via Bedrock) | [AWS HIPAA eligible services reference](https://aws.amazon.com/compliance/hipaa-eligible-services-reference/) |
| 1.11.3.8 | **GCP (Vertex AI, Gemini):** not researched this session. | ⚠️ | — (Topic 5) |
| 1.11.3.9 | **Relation to the owner decision (inference):** under the owner's default, PHI never reaches the agent, so none of 1.11.3.3–1.11.3.7 is needed for the DevSecOps agent. `work/01-problem-framing.md` GĐ-9 allows case-by-case approved reads of real data with "BAA/DPA". 1.11.3.4–1.11.3.5 show that on the current Team plan, that exception **cannot include PHI sent to Claude**: no BAA covers it. That would need the separate Enterprise + BAA environment named in the owner decision. GĐ-9 and its consequences should be checked against this when the design is written. | ⚠️ inference | — |

#### 1.11.4 Paths by which PHI can reach a DevSecOps agent's context (to handle in Phase 4)

**This is my analysis, not quoted from any document.** It lists paths to close or control, so that
"PHI never reaches the agent" holds. "Context" includes anything the agent reads: tool output, files,
fetched pages, MCP results, images. Anything in context is sent to the model provider and saved in
the local session transcript (`~/.claude*/projects/…/*.jsonl`, **local check** on this machine).
Controls are only candidates; they are designed in Phase 4.

| # | Path | How it gets into context | Why PHI is likely | Candidate controls (Phase 4) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | **Prod logs:** CloudWatch Logs from Lambda and ECS, k0s pod logs, GCP Cloud Logging | Agent runs `aws logs`, `kubectl logs`, or reads a log MCP during debug or incident | Request payloads, exception messages with record values, document-extraction output, IPs (identifier) | Log redaction at source; agent role reads metrics and redacted log groups only; separate log group for raw payloads with no agent access |
| L2 | **Database queries:** Aurora prod or replicas | `psql` or a DB MCP; `SELECT *` while debugging; error messages and slow-query or `pg_stat_statements` text with literals | Claim tables hold MED + NID + BANK | No DB credentials for the agent; a schema-only or masked view role; reads of real data only through the GĐ-9 exception |
| L3 | **S3:** claim documents, exports, backups | `aws s3 cp/ls`; reading a file to "check format" | Medical documents and ID scans; **object keys** may contain names or ID numbers | Deny `s3:GetObject` on PHI buckets for agent roles; consider whether `ListBucket` exposes keys |
| L4 | **Message and workflow payloads:** SQS/DLQ, SNS, Step Functions execution history | Inspecting a DLQ or execution input/output during an incident | Payloads carry claim data; Step Functions stores input/output in history | Same as L3 for `sqs:ReceiveMessage` and `states:GetExecutionHistory`; payloads carry references, not data |
| L5 | **Tickets and chat:** Linear, Slack (incl. via MCP connectors) | Agent reads an issue or thread linked from a task | Support escalations paste claim details and screenshots | Ticket hygiene rule (no PHI in tickets); scope or deny those MCP connectors; redaction bot |
| L6 | **Partner and member uploaded documents** while debugging prod AI agents (A7b in problem framing) | Engineer gives the agent a failing document to reproduce a bug | The document **is** PHI, and is also an injection vector | Reproduce with synthetic documents; a de-identification step before any document reaches the coding agent |
| L7 | **Non-prod data that is not synthetic** | Agent works freely in dev/staging (GĐ-14) | If a prod copy or dump exists in staging, PHI is there | Enforce GĐ-14: no prod → non-prod copies; scan non-prod stores |
| L8 | **Repo content:** fixtures, seed files, sample documents, notebooks committed from real data | Agent reads the repo (always) | Engineers copy "a real example" into tests | Secret/PII scanning in CI and pre-commit; review rule for fixtures |

#### 1.11.4 Paths by which PHI can reach a DevSecOps agent's context (to handle in Phase 4)

**This is my analysis, not quoted from any document.** It lists paths to close or control, so that
"PHI never reaches the agent" holds. "Context" includes anything the agent reads: tool output, files,
fetched pages, MCP results, images. Anything in context is sent to the model provider and saved in
the local session transcript (`~/.claude*/projects/…/*.jsonl`, **local check** on this machine).
Controls are only candidates; they are designed in Phase 4.

| # | Path | How it gets into context | Why PHI is likely | Candidate controls (Phase 4) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | **Prod logs:** CloudWatch Logs from Lambda and ECS, k0s pod logs, GCP Cloud Logging | Agent runs `aws logs`, `kubectl logs`, or reads a log MCP during debug or incident | Request payloads, exception messages with record values, document-extraction output, IPs (identifier) | Log redaction at source; agent role reads metrics and redacted log groups only; separate log group for raw payloads with no agent access |
| L2 | **Database queries:** Aurora prod or replicas | `psql` or a DB MCP; `SELECT *` while debugging; error messages and slow-query or `pg_stat_statements` text with literals | Claim tables hold MED + NID + BANK | No DB credentials for the agent; a schema-only or masked view role; reads of real data only through the GĐ-9 exception |
| L3 | **S3:** claim documents, exports, backups | `aws s3 cp/ls`; reading a file to "check format" | Medical documents and ID scans; **object keys** may contain names or ID numbers | Deny `s3:GetObject` on PHI buckets for agent roles; consider whether `ListBucket` exposes keys |
| L4 | **Message and workflow payloads:** SQS/DLQ, SNS, Step Functions execution history | Inspecting a DLQ or execution input/output during an incident | Payloads carry claim data; Step Functions stores input/output in history | Same as L3 for `sqs:ReceiveMessage` and `states:GetExecutionHistory`; payloads carry references, not data |
| L5 | **Tickets and chat:** Linear, Slack (incl. via MCP connectors) | Agent reads an issue or thread linked from a task | Support escalations paste claim details and screenshots | Ticket hygiene rule (no PHI in tickets); scope or deny those MCP connectors; redaction bot |
| L6 | **Partner and member uploaded documents** while debugging prod AI agents (A7b in problem framing) | Engineer gives the agent a failing document to reproduce a bug | The document **is** PHI, and is also an injection vector | Reproduce with synthetic documents; a de-identification step before any document reaches the coding agent |
| L7 | **Non-prod data that is not synthetic** | Agent works freely in dev/staging (GĐ-14) | If a prod copy or dump exists in staging, PHI is there | Enforce GĐ-14: no prod → non-prod copies; scan non-prod stores |
| L8 | **Repo content:** fixtures, seed files, sample documents, notebooks committed from real data | Agent reads the repo (always) | Engineers copy "a real example" into tests | Secret/PII scanning in CI and pre-commit; review rule for fixtures |
| L9 | **CI output:** GitHub Actions logs and artifacts from jobs that touch real data | Agent reads CI logs to fix a failing job | Test or migration output that prints rows | No real data in CI; log masking |
| L10 | **What humans paste:** text, screenshots or files pasted into the chat by the engineer | Direct input | Copying from an admin console or a customer email | Training and a clear rule; a `UserPromptSubmit` hook pattern check (weak, advisory) |
| L11 | **Prod shell access:** `kubectl exec`, ECS Exec, SSM on EC2 | Agent runs commands inside a prod workload | Env vars, mounted files and local caches hold data or DB credentials | No exec rights for agent roles in prod |
| L12 | **Fetched web content:** internal dashboards and admin UIs reachable from the laptop | WebFetch or browser tools | Admin pages show member records | Network or domain allowlist; deny fetch to internal admin hosts |

Cross-cutting point (inference): every path above depends on **what the agent's identity is allowed
to read**. So the strongest single control for the owner decision is an agent identity with **no
data-plane read on PHI stores**: IAM, DB roles and k0s RBAC (Topics 2–3). Redaction and rules on
the Claude Code side are the second layer, consistent with 1.8 #1.

  **M1 — MEDIUM — 1.11.3.5 (Console API key): thiếu điều kiện**
  - Vấn đề: câu trích "covered through ZDR, not through the HIPAA configuration" bị bỏ mất điều kiện đi kèm.
  - Bằng chứng: trang BAA chỉ cho dòng này áp dụng khi Console organization đã bật zero data retention. Không có ZDR thì "not covered". `hipaa-setup` cũng ghi: "These sessions belong to a Claude Console organization, which has its own agreement and settings".

  - Bằng chứng: phần có nguồn là trang BAA của Anthropic ghi "⚠️ Not covered. Claude Code (local mode) is covered only when Claude Code connects directly to Anthropic". Không nguồn nào nói AWS BAA phủ phiên Claude Code chạy qua Bedrock.
  - Đề xuất: viết lại thành hai câu. Câu ✅: "Anthropic BAA không phủ Claude Code qua Bedrock". Câu ⚠️: "Bedrock nằm trong danh sách AWS eligible; việc AWS BAA có phủ toàn bộ luồng dữ liệu của Claude Code hay không thì chưa kiểm chứng".
  
  **M3 — MEDIUM — 1.11.3.9: kết luận quá mạnh, thiếu một hướng thay thế**
  - Vấn đề: câu "That would need the separate Enterprise + BAA environment" bỏ qua một hướng khác mà nguồn có nêu.
  - Bằng chứng: trang BAA ghi BAA phủ cả "first-party API", và với API thì "Primary Owner will need to sign a BAA and then reach out to … Sales". Câu "Team không được phủ" vẫn là ⚠️ (trang không nhắc tới Team).
  - Đề xuất: liệt kê đủ các hướng gửi PHI tới Claude: Enterprise + HIPAA config, API org có BAA (với Claude Code thì phải qua ZDR như M1), và Bedrock + AWS BAA (⚠️). Ghi rõ "Team chưa có nguồn khẳng định phủ" là ⚠️ cần hỏi Anthropic.
  
  **M4 — MEDIUM — mục đã chốt đầu tiên trong 1.9 và 1.11.3: chưa ghi xung đột giữa ZDR và Covered Models**
  - Vấn đề: mục đã chốt vẫn mô tả hướng thay thế là "Enterprise + BAA + ZDR". Trang BAA lại nói Covered Models cần 30-day retention. Owner chỉ nói "Enterprise + BAA".
  - Bằng chứng: "Covered Models require 30-day data retention and aren't available with zero data retention (ZDR) enabled" ("unless Anthropic has expressly authorized it").
  - Đề xuất: thêm một dòng 1.11.3.x ✅ về điều này. Trong mục 1.9, ghi chú rằng câu hỏi gốc nhắc ZDR nhưng quyết định của owner thì không, và ZDR có thể xung đột với Covered Models. Không sửa câu trích của owner.
  
  **M5 — MEDIUM — 1.11.4: thiếu các leak path quan trọng của stack hiện tại**
  - (a) Kho dữ liệu GCP gửi sang Vertex/Gemini: GCS, dataset, log request/response của Vertex. L1 mới chỉ nhắc Cloud Logging, trong khi A4 nói tài liệu được gửi sang GCP.
  - (b) Trace, prompt log và output của các AI agent prod (claim assessment, extraction, FWA) ở OpenAI, Vertex hoặc Claude. Agent prod nào cũng có loại này, và chúng chứa PHI. L6 chỉ nói tới tài liệu upload.
  - (c) CloudTrail data events, S3 access logs, Athena hoặc CloudWatch Logs Insights trên dữ liệu đó, và Aurora snapshot/export (trừ trường hợp restore sang non-prod, đã có ở L7).
  - (d) Payload Lambda đọc qua test event, `aws lambda invoke` hoặc replay khi debug.
  - (e) Alert trong Slack nhúng nguyên dòng log. L5 mới nói tới ticket do người dán vào.
  - Đề xuất: thêm các dòng L13 trở đi. Thêm một đoạn ngắn về chỗ PHI đi tiếp sau khi đã vào context: auto-memory/CLAUDE.md, commit, PR, comment trên Linear. `hipaa-setup` có câu "Your BAA with Anthropic doesn't cover the data it sends there".
  
  **L1 — LOW — 1.11.3.1: câu trích bị cắt**
  - Bằng chứng: văn bản gốc 164.502(e)(2) là "written contract or other written agreement **or arrangement**".
  - Đề xuất: trích đủ câu.

Gắn vào câu hỏi pháp lý ở 1.11.1.11.

  - Vấn đề: dòng được đánh [x], nhưng sự thật "Papaya có MDM hay không" vẫn chưa biết. Cái đã chốt là cách thiết kế (chuẩn bị cho cả hai).
  - Đề xuất: ghi rõ phần đã chốt là cách thiết kế, và để lại một việc mở nhỏ: hỏi Papaya về MDM.
  
  **L8 — LOW — 1.11.3.5: chữ "available" chưa đủ**
  - Bằng chứng: trang BAA về connector ghi "Your BAA doesn't cover any of them, even after an Owner turns them on". Nghĩa là connector có thể bị tắt dưới HIPAA config.
  - Đề xuất: sửa câu cho chính xác.

  - BAA "only covers the single organization that accepted it", và loại trừ Claude Console và Cowork in the cloud. Điểm này ủng hộ ý "môi trường riêng" trong quyết định của owner.

Trang AWS ghi ngày "Last Updated: October 15, 2026", và cả 5 dịch vụ được nêu đều có trong danh sách. Không thấy secret hay dữ liệu cá nhân.

### Findings

**M1 — MEDIUM — 1.11.3.5 (Console API key): thiếu điều kiện**
- Vấn đề: câu trích "covered through ZDR, not through the HIPAA configuration" bị bỏ mất điều kiện đi kèm.
- Bằng chứng: trang BAA chỉ cho dòng này áp dụng khi Console organization đã bật zero data retention. Không có ZDR thì "not covered". `hipaa-setup` cũng ghi: "These sessions belong to a Claude Console organization, which has its own agreement and settings".
- Đề xuất: thêm "chỉ khi Console org bật ZDR; không có ZDR thì không được bảo vệ; đây là org riêng với agreement riêng". Điều kiện này quan trọng cho agent chạy CI bằng API key (1.7).

**M2 — MEDIUM — 1.11.3.7: suy luận viết như sự thật**

- Bằng chứng: phần có nguồn là trang BAA của Anthropic ghi "⚠️ Not covered. Claude Code (local mode) is covered only when Claude Code connects directly to Anthropic". Không nguồn nào nói AWS BAA phủ phiên Claude Code chạy qua Bedrock.
- Đề xuất: viết lại thành hai câu. Câu ✅: "Anthropic BAA không phủ Claude Code qua Bedrock". Câu ⚠️: "Bedrock nằm trong danh sách AWS eligible; việc AWS BAA có phủ toàn bộ luồng dữ liệu của Claude Code hay không thì chưa kiểm chứng".

**M3 — MEDIUM — 1.11.3.9: kết luận quá mạnh, thiếu một hướng thay thế**
- Vấn đề: câu "That would need the separate Enterprise + BAA environment" bỏ qua một hướng khác mà nguồn có nêu.
- Bằng chứng: trang BAA ghi BAA phủ cả "first-party API", và với API thì "Primary Owner will need to sign a BAA and then reach out to … Sales". Câu "Team không được phủ" vẫn là ⚠️ (trang không nhắc tới Team).

**M4 — MEDIUM — mục đã chốt đầu tiên trong 1.9 và 1.11.3: chưa ghi xung đột giữa ZDR và Covered Models**

- (a) Kho dữ liệu GCP gửi sang Vertex/Gemini: GCS, dataset, log request/response của Vertex. L1 mới chỉ nhắc Cloud Logging, trong khi A4 nói tài liệu được gửi sang GCP.

Health plan cũng loại trừ "excepted benefits" (160.103, Health plan (2)(i)). Hai điểm này liên quan nếu đối tác là life insurer hoặc dùng sản phẩm Underwriting. Gắn vào câu hỏi pháp lý ở 1.11.1.11.

- Vấn đề: 18 identifier là phép thử de-identification cho thông tin sức khoẻ, không phải phép thử để biết dữ liệu không liên quan sức khoẻ có phải PHI không. Một IP đứng riêng trong log hạ tầng chưa phải PHI. IP gắn với URL có claim ID thì có thể là PHI.

input.old_string: | L12 | **Fetched web content:** internal dashboards and admin UIs reachable from the laptop | WebFetch or browser tools | Admin pages show member records | Network or domain allowlist; deny fetch to internal admin hosts |
input.new_string:
| L12 | **Fetched web content:** internal dashboards and admin UIs reachable from the laptop | WebFetch or browser tools | Admin pages show member records | Network or domain allowlist; deny fetch to internal admin hosts |
| L13 | **GCP data stores** that feed Vertex AI / Gemini: GCS buckets, datasets, Vertex request/response logging | `gcloud`/`gsutil` or a GCP MCP while debugging the AI pipeline | Medical documents are sent to GCP for extraction (A4/A13 in problem framing) | Same model as L3 on the GCP side: no data-plane read for agent identities; GCP BAA status ⚠️ (1.11.3.8) |
| L14 | **Prod AI agent traces:** prompt/response logs, traces and evaluation sets of claim assessment, extraction and FWA agents (OpenAI, Vertex, Claude) | Agent reads traces to debug a model or prompt regression | Prompts and outputs contain the claim and document content | Traces stored as PHI with restricted access; debug with redacted or synthetic traces |
| L15 | **Secondary copies on AWS:** CloudTrail data events, S3 access logs, Athena or CloudWatch Logs Insights results, Aurora snapshots and exports | Queries run for audit or incident analysis; restoring a snapshot to inspect it | Data events and query results can include object keys and record values; snapshots are full copies | Treat these stores as PHI-bearing; no snapshot restore or export rights for agent roles |
| L16 | **Lambda payload replay:** test events, `aws lambda invoke`, replaying a failed event | Agent copies a real event to reproduce a bug | The event is the real claim payload | Replay only with synthetic or redacted events; no `lambda:InvokeFunction` on prod for agent roles |
| L17 | **Automated alerts in Slack** that embed raw log lines or payloads | Agent reads an alert channel or thread via MCP | Alert bots paste the failing record | Alerts carry IDs and links, not payloads (ties to P6) |

**Where PHI goes next once it is in context (analysis).** The agent can write it to places that
last longer than the session and are outside any Anthropic BAA:
- auto-memory and `CLAUDE.md` files;
- commits, PR descriptions and code comments;
- Linear comments and Slack messages;
- CI logs.

hipaa-setup says of data sent to GitHub or other services: "Your BAA with Anthropic doesn't cover
the data it sends there" (1.11.3.6). So a leak into context is not only a model-provider issue; it
can turn into a persistent copy. Phase 4 should cover these outflows as well as the inflows above.

Đã kiểm lại với bản eCFR tải sẵn, `hipaa-setup.md`, và trang BAA của Anthropic (WebFetch lần nữa, lấy câu chữ nguyên văn cho các câu trích mới). Không sửa file nào. Blockquote của owner trong 1.9 giống hệt round 1.

### Trạng thái các finding round 1

| Finding | Trạng thái | Bằng chứng |
|---|---|---|
| M1: Console API key cần ZDR | FIXED | Khớp nguyên văn trang BAA: "when the Claude Console organization has zero data retention (ZDR) enabled" và "✅ Covered through ZDR, not through the HIPAA configuration". Không có ZDR thì "⚠️ Not covered". |

### Finding mới

**N1 — LOW — 1.11.3.11 và 1.11.3.5: hai dòng có vẻ mâu thuẫn**
- Vấn đề: 1.11.3.11 ghi "Claude Console is excluded", còn 1.11.3.5 lại nói phiên Console API key được phủ qua ZDR. Người đọc sẽ thấy hai dòng trái nhau.
- Bằng chứng: trang BAA ghi BAA "excludes features such as Claude Console, Cowork in the cloud, or features currently in beta such as Claude in Office, Claude Design, Claude Slides, and Claude Docs". Cùng trang đó lại liệt kê dòng Console-API-key-with-ZDR là "Covered through ZDR".
- Đề xuất: ghi rằng "Claude Console" ở đây có vẻ là sản phẩm/giao diện Console, không phải API usage qua ZDR. Đánh ⚠️ cho cách hiểu này và ghi mâu thuẫn nằm ngay trong nguồn. Có thể trích đủ danh sách loại trừ.

**N2 — LOW — 1.11.3.11: tham chiếu chéo sai**
- Vấn đề: câu "minimum version, `allowedProviders`, `forceLoginOrgUUID` … are in 1.1 and 1.6.7" không đúng hết.
- Bằng chứng: grep cho thấy `forceLoginOrgUUID` chỉ có ở 1.8 (dòng 177) và 1.11.3.11, không có trong 1.1 hay 1.6.7. `requiredMinimumVersion` ở 1.1.13. `allowedProviders` ở 1.1.15.
- Đề xuất: đổi thành "1.1.13, 1.1.15, 1.8 #…". Hoặc trích `forceLoginOrgUUID` thẳng từ hipaa-setup và đánh ✅.

**N3 — LOW — 1.11.3.9(b): "conflicts with Covered Models" thiếu qualifier**
- Vấn đề: viết như thể ZDR luôn xung đột. Thực ra trong route ZDR, Covered Models chỉ không dùng được nếu Anthropic chưa cho phép riêng.
- Đề xuất: viết "Covered Models are unavailable under ZDR unless Anthropic authorizes it (1.11.3.10)".

**N4 — LOW — L13: "for extraction" không có trong framing**
- Vấn đề: A4 trong `01-problem-framing.md` chỉ nói tài liệu được gửi sang GCP "để xử lý", không nói "extraction".
- Đề xuất: viết "for processing", hoặc ghi rõ "extraction" là suy luận.

**N5 — LOW — đoạn outflow: "outside any Anthropic BAA" không đúng với file local**
- Vấn đề: auto-memory và `CLAUDE.md` là file local, không phải bên thứ ba.
- Bằng chứng: hipaa-setup chỉ nói dữ liệu local là "your organization's responsibility".
- Đề xuất: viết "outside the session and, for GitHub/Linear/Slack/CI, outside the Anthropic BAA". Ghi thêm rằng memory/CLAUDE.md có thể bị commit lên git.

### Coverage gap còn lại (nhỏ)
- 1.7.6 nêu workload identity federation cho CI. hipaa-setup ghi federation credentials là "No" cho HIPAA config, và trang BAA không nói route này có được phủ qua ZDR hay không. Nên thêm một dòng ⚠️ nếu CI agent có thể chạm tới PHI. Theo quyết định của owner thì không chặn gì.

### Các phần mới khác đã kiểm, không có lỗi
1.11.1.10, 1.11.1.11, 1.11.1.12, 1.11.3.1, 1.11.3.2, 1.11.3.7, 1.11.3.10, L1, L14–L17, các item trong 1.9. Ở log 1.10, số đếm của round 1 (0 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 8 LOW / 6 gaps) là đúng.

**Where PHI goes next once it is in context (analysis).** The agent can write it to places that
-last longer than the session and are outside any Anthropic BAA:
-- auto-memory and `CLAUDE.md` files;
+last longer than the session:
+- auto-memory and `CLAUDE.md` files: local, the organization's responsibility, and they can end up
+  committed to git;
- commits, PR descriptions and code comments;
- Linear comments and Slack messages;
- CI logs.
+GitHub, Linear, Slack and CI are third parties, outside the Anthropic BAA.
hipaa-setup says of data sent to GitHub or other services: "Your BAA with Anthropic doesn't cover
the data it sends there" (1.11.3.6). So a leak into context is not only a model-provider issue; it
can turn into a persistent copy. Phase 4 should cover these outflows as well as the inflows above.

**Diff:** `work/02-research.md` đang là file untracked, nên `git diff` không hiện gì. Mình ghép lại bản trước khi sửa (giữ nguyên dòng 1–195, cộng nguyên văn mục 1.9–1.10 cũ) rồi so với bản hiện tại. Kết quả: 164 dòng thêm, 3 dòng xoá. Hunk đầu tiên bắt đầu ở dòng 197, nên **mục 1.1–1.8 không bị đụng tới**. Diff đầy đủ: `/tmp/claude-1001/-home-do-hoang-minh-hung-papaya-devsecops-challenge/2e770088-3c42-4cef-b063-5c554b20a853/scratchpad/1.11.diff`

Ba mục còn mở (`--bare`, sudo trên runner, audit log trên gói Team) vẫn giữ nguyên. Riêng câu hỏi MDM, mình tách thành hai dòng: cách thiết kế thì bạn đã chốt, còn việc Papaya có dùng MDM hay không vẫn là câu hỏi mở. Bạn xem cách tách này có đúng ý không.

Mục 1.10 thêm một dòng: owner đã chốt mục PHI và MDM, mục 1.11 được thêm theo yêu cầu, 1.1–1.8 không đổi. Kèm theo là log hai vòng review của 1.11:
- Vòng 1: 0 HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 8 LOW, 6 chỗ còn thiếu. Mình kiểm lại với nguồn, tất cả đều đúng và đã sửa.
- Vòng 2: 0 HIGH, 0 MEDIUM, 5 LOW, đã sửa hết.

**Mục 1.11** chỉ có thêm, không sửa gì cũ. Bạn đọc trực tiếp trong [work/02-research.md](work/02-research.md) từ dòng 268. Gồm 4 phần:
- **1.11.1 Định nghĩa:** PHI, IIHI, covered entity, business associate, payment, de-identification (18 identifier), minimum necessary, PII. Tất cả ✅, trích từ văn bản luật 45 CFR. Có hai dòng ⚠️:
  - HIPAA có thực sự áp dụng cho Papaya không: đây là câu hỏi pháp lý.
  - Luật khu vực: chỉ tìm được nguồn thứ cấp.
- **1.11.2 Phân loại dữ liệu Papaya:** hồ sơ bệnh, chẩn đoán và lịch sử claim là PHI. CCCD và tài khoản ngân hàng là PII khi đứng riêng, nhưng thành một phần của PHI khi nằm trong bản ghi claim. Toàn bộ bảng này là suy luận (⚠️).
- **1.11.3 Điều kiện để nhà cung cấp model được xử lý PHI:** gồm yêu cầu BAA theo luật, phạm vi BAA của Anthropic, và danh sách HIPAA-eligible của AWS.
- **1.11.4 Danh sách L1–L17:** các đường PHI có thể lọt vào context của agent, cộng một đoạn về chỗ PHI đi tiếp sau khi đã vào context. Phần này ghi rõ là phân tích, để xử lý ở Phase 4.

**Bạn nên biết thêm:**
1. **HHS.gov chặn truy cập tự động (lỗi 403).** Mình không đọc được trang nào của HHS, nên mọi khẳng định trong 1.11 dựa trên văn bản luật gốc 45 CFR trên eCFR (đọc qua API chính thức). Link HHS vẫn có trong file nhưng đánh 📖 và ghi "403, not read". Bạn nên mở tay vài trang HHS để đối chiếu.
2. **Quyết định của bạn và GĐ-9 có điểm vênh** (dòng 1.11.3.9, suy luận). GĐ-9 trong `01-problem-framing.md` cho phép đọc dữ liệu thật theo từng trường hợp, có duyệt. Nhưng trên gói Team hiện tại, không có BAA nào cho phép PHI đi tới Claude. Vì vậy ngoại lệ đó chỉ có thể dùng trong môi trường Enterprise + BAA riêng như bạn đã nêu. Mình chưa sửa GĐ-9; nên rà lại khi viết design.
3. **Nếu sau này dựng môi trường BAA, không thể bật ZDR rồi coi là xong.**

+## Topic 1 — Claude Code at organization level
+**Accessed:** 2026-11-08. Pages (all under `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/`, also read as raw

+### 1.1 Configuration users cannot override ("managed settings")
+| # | Finding | Marker | Source |

+| 1.1.1 | Precedence, highest first: **managed** → command line (`--settings`) → project local (`.claude/settings.local.json`) → shared project (`.claude/settings.json`) → user (`~/.claude/settings.json`). "Nothing in your own settings files or `--settings` overrides a managed key." | ✅ | [settings#settings-precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence) |

+| 1.1.2 | List keys (e.g. `permissions.allow`) **merge** across scopes rather than override; deny from any scope beats allow from any scope. "A managed settings deny can't be overridden by `--allowedTools`." | ✅ | [settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#lists-merge-instead-of-overriding), [permissions#settings-precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#settings-precedence) |

+| 1.1.3 | Four delivery mechanisms: **server-managed** (claude.ai admin console, fetched at startup, polled hourly), **MDM/OS policy** (macOS profile domain `com.anthropic.claudecode`, Windows `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode`, checked every 30 min), **file** (`/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` on Linux/WSL, `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/` on macOS, `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\` on Windows, plus a `managed-settings.d/` drop-in dir), **HKCU registry** (lowest). | ✅ | [managed-settings#choose-a-delivery-mechanism](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#choose-a-delivery-mechanism) |

+| 1.1.4 | By default only **one** managed source supplies most keys (server-managed first, then MDM, then file); `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` composes them. **Exceptions:** "cross-source keys" are read from every admin source, e.g. `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, `deniedMcpServers`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`, the sandbox managed-only locks, `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`, and `env` (merged per variable). `allowedProviders` has its own rule (machine list and server list intersect). `managed-mcp.json` is read separately from the settings tier. | ✅ | [managed-settings#keys-read-from-every-admin-source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-read-from-every-admin-source), [plugins/org](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/org#which-managed-source-applies-on-a-machine) |

+| 1.1.5 | **Server-managed settings are available on Claude for Teams and Enterprise**; editing needs the **Owner / Primary Owner** role. Relevant: Papaya is on Team Premium. | ✅ | [server-managed-settings#requirements](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#requirements) |

+| 1.1.6 | Server-managed limitations: settings apply **uniformly to the whole org** (no per-group policy yet); `managed-mcp.json` cannot be delivered this way. Per-group policy is possible with separate endpoint files/profiles, or with a self-hosted **Claude apps gateway**, which "delivers managed settings per IdP group". | ✅ | [server-managed-settings#current-limitations](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#current-limitations), [managed-settings#choose-a-delivery-mechanism](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#choose-a-delivery-mechanism) |

+| 1.1.7 | Docs state plainly that server-managed settings are "**a client-side control, not a security boundary**. On unmanaged devices, a user doesn't need admin or sudo access to bypass them." Bypass cases listed: editing/deleting the local cache, modified or older binary, **authenticating with a different org or a Console API key**, or **setting a `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` provider variable** (`…_BEDROCK`, `…_VERTEX`, `…_MANTLE`, `…_FOUNDRY`, `…_ANTHROPIC_AWS`) **or a non-default `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`**. | ✅ | [server-managed-settings#security-considerations](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-considerations) |

+| 1.1.8 | Endpoint-managed (MDM/file) "provide stronger security guarantees because the settings file can be protected from user modification at the OS level", but a developer with **local admin** can still edit the managed source; managed settings "bind Claude Code only" — another API client is not covered. | ✅ | [server-managed-settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#choose-between-server-managed-and-endpoint-managed-settings), [managed-settings#what-a-developer-can-change](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#what-a-developer-can-change) |

+| 1.1.9 | `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true` makes startup **fail closed**: the CLI blocks until a fresh fetch succeeds and exits if it fails. **Caveats:** it does not close the 1.1.7 bypasses — "A session that doesn't fetch server-managed settings starts without waiting"; and if `api.anthropic.com` is unreachable, nobody can start Claude Code. | ✅ | [server-managed-settings#enforce-fail-closed-startup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#enforce-fail-closed-startup) |

+| 1.1.10 | Server-delivered **hooks, shell-command settings, some `env` vars and sandbox-weakening keys** show a security approval dialog **in interactive sessions**; if the user rejects, Claude Code exits. In a non-interactive run (`claude -p`, Agent SDK, VS Code chat panel, desktop Code tab) "Claude Code can't show the dialog. When the delivered settings would require approval, they apply for that run only." A managed `claudeMd` value needs no approval. | ✅ | [server-managed-settings#security-approval-dialogs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#security-approval-dialogs) |

+| 1.1.11 | Invalid managed entries: many locks **fail closed** (e.g. an unreadable `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` reads as its restrictive value; an unreadable `deny` list withholds `allow`), from v2.1.282. **Fail-open cases also exist:** "`requiredMinimumVersion` and `requiredMaximumVersion` fail open by design"; an invalid `disableAllHooks` is dropped; and "If the operating system denied the read, for example on a root-only file, every session starts without that source's policies" (recorded only in `/status` / `claude doctor`). ⇒ A wrongly-permissioned policy file silently removes the policy. | ✅ | [managed-settings#keys-that-fail-closed](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-that-fail-closed), [managed-settings#find-entries-claude-code-dropped](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#find-entries-claude-code-dropped) |

+| 1.1.12 | Audit events for settings changes (who, which device, old/new value) exist "through the compliance API or audit log export. Contact your Anthropic account team for access." | ✅ (exists) / ⚠️ (availability on **Team** plan not stated — ask Anthropic) | [server-managed-settings#audit-logging](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings#audit-logging) |

+| 1.1.13 | `requiredMinimumVersion` (and `requiredMaximumVersion`) blocks a binary outside the range from starting; does not end a running session; an invalid value fails open. | ✅ | [managed-settings#where-and-when-a-policy-applies](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#where-and-when-a-policy-applies), [managed-settings#keys-that-fail-closed](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-that-fail-closed) |

+| 1.1.14 | A few security keys honour a **stricter** value from a lower scope even over managed (e.g. `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories: true`, `permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories: true` (v2.1.314+), `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true`). Users can tighten, not loosen. | ✅ | [settings#exceptions-to-managed-settings-precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#exceptions-to-managed-settings-precedence) |

+| 1.1.15 | **`allowedProviders`** (managed, v2.1.285+) lists which providers a machine may use (`anthropic`, `bedrock`, `vertex`, `foundry`, `anthropicAws`, `mantle`, `customEndpoint`, `gateway`); "A session on a provider that isn't listed is refused at startup, at login, and when it next contacts the API". A list from MDM/file keeps applying when server-managed settings also send one ("can narrow … but never widen"). Pair with `forceLoginOrgUUID` / `forceLoginMethod` to pin sign-in to Papaya's org. ⇒ On endpoint-managed machines this closes most of the 1.1.7 bypasses. | ✅ | [settings-reference#allowedproviders](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#allowedproviders), [settings-reference#forceloginorguuid](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceloginorguuid) |

+| 1.1.16 | **Managed instructions:** key `claudeMd` (managed scope) injects organization-wide CLAUDE.md text "ahead of user and project CLAUDE.md files". It is instruction text, not enforcement. | ✅ | [settings-reference#claudemd](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#claudemd) |

+| 1.1.17 | A managed `model` "is a starting default, not a lock"; the locks are `availableModels` and `deniedModels`. | ✅ | [settings#settings-precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence) |

+| 1.1.18 | Proving a policy is in force: `/status` shows `Setting sources` (and the managed source); `claude doctor` lists dropped entries and an `Organization policy` line (v2.1.261+). Useful as audit evidence. | ✅ | [managed-settings#check-that-a-policy-is-in-force](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#check-that-a-policy-is-in-force), [managed-settings#keys-only-a-managed-source-can-set](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-only-a-managed-source-can-set) |

+| 1.1.19 | On Team/Enterprise an Owner turns **Remote Control** and **cloud sessions** on/off org-wide; `disableRemoteControl` disables Remote Control per device. Cloud sessions in Anthropic-hosted environments receive **only server-managed** settings. | ✅ | [managed-settings#keys-only-a-managed-source-can-set](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-only-a-managed-source-can-set) (note), [managed-settings#where-and-when-a-policy-applies](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#where-and-when-a-policy-applies) |

+| 1.1.20 | **Telemetry is not a tamper-proof audit log:** OTel exporter selectors follow normal precedence and "A developer's setting can still disable a signal … so set the selectors in managed settings too". | ✅ | [monitoring-usage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage) |

+| 1.1.21 | Server-managed settings page recommends network-level **Tenant Restrictions** to stop sign-in to other Claude orgs. | 📖 (support article not opened) | [support.claude.com/…/13198485](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13198485) |

+### 1.8 What this means for Papaya (inferences — to be used in the design)
+These are my conclusions from the findings above, not documented facts:
+1. **Policy layer exists and is real, but it is client-side.** Managed settings can lock bypass/auto
+   mode, MCP, plugins and hooks (1.1, 1.2). The docs themselves say it is not a security boundary
+   (1.1.7, 1.1.8), and some failure modes are silent (1.1.11). ⇒ Compliance's rule ("named human
+   approves prod changes") **cannot rest on Claude Code settings**. It must be enforced where the
+   agent cannot reach: AWS IAM / GitHub (Topics 2–3). Claude Code settings are a *safety and
+   hygiene* layer (fewer mistakes), not the control of record.
+2. **Team plan is enough for the technical policy layer, not for PHI.** Team has server-managed
+   settings (1.1.5) but not the HIPAA configuration/BAA (1.6.7), ZDR (1.6.8) or the Analytics API
+   (1.4.6); settings-change audit on Team is uncertain (1.1.12). ⇒ Either the design guarantees
+   that **agents never see PHI/production data** (fits Topic-0 scope: non-prod is synthetic), or
+   Papaya moves to Enterprise + BAA. This is a decision for Papaya (open item).
+3. **Two delivery paths are needed:** server-managed for laptops; an endpoint `managed-settings.json`
+   (+ `managed-mcp.json` if exclusive MCP control is wanted, + `allowedProviders`/`forceLoginOrgUUID`
+   to close provider bypasses, 1.1.15) on every machine that runs an agent unattended, because
+   server-managed settings do not reach CI (1.7.10) and are skipped when a provider env var is set
+   (1.1.7). On **GitHub-hosted runners** there is no image to bake into: the file would be written
+   by a workflow step, and the agent step must not be able to rewrite it (⚠️ depends on whether the
+   agent step has sudo — check in Topic 3). Self-hosted runners or a container image are cleaner.
+4. **Defaults are permissive for this context:** interactive sessions start in auto mode, where a
+   classifier — not a human — approves routine actions (1.2.3); sandbox is off (1.6.1); hooks fail
+   open (1.5.2); `-p` runs execute repo hooks, `env` and helpers and connect `.mcp.json` (1.7.3).
+   Each needs an explicit org setting (`disableAutoMode`, `sandbox.enabled`, `onFailure: "block"`,
+   `--setting-sources`/`disableAllHooks` in CI).
+5. **Bash deny rules are advisory** (1.2.6), and the sandbox covers only shell commands (1.6.2).
+   Keeping prod credentials away from the agent needs several layers: sandbox
+   `denyRead`/`credentials` for Bash, `Read(...)` deny rules and `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`
+   for file tools, env scrub (which keeps GitHub tokens, 1.6.5), or the whole process in a
+   container (1.6.6). The decisive layer is still **no prod credentials on the agent's machine at
+   all**, plus IAM on the AWS side.
