## Choosing a state backend

Pulumi supports two classes of state backend:

- **Pulumi Cloud**: a managed backend using the online or self-hosted Pulumi Cloud application. Pulumi Cloud is the default backend: after [installing the CLI](/docs/install/), the CLI prompts you to sign in the first time you run `pulumi login`.
- **DIY backend**: a "Do It Yourself" backend that stores state in an object store you manage—AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, an S3-compatible server such as Minio or Ceph, a PostgreSQL database, or your local filesystem.

Pulumi's SDK works with all backends, although some details differ between them. For a full comparison of the two options—including the operational concerns each one entails—see [Pulumi Cloud vs. OSS](/docs/iac/guides/basics/pulumi-cloud-vs-oss/). For DIY backend setup instructions, see [Using a DIY backend](/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/).

## Pulumi Cloud backend
> This [Pulumi Cloud](/docs/iac/concepts/pulumi-cloud/) feature is available in [all editions](/pricing/).
When you're logged out, running `pulumi login` without any argument logs into the default Pulumi Cloud backend:
```sh
$ pulumi login
```
This displays a prompt that asks for an [access token](/docs/administration/concepts/access-tokens/):
```
Manage your Pulumi stacks by logging in.
Run `pulumi login --help` for alternative login options.
Enter your access token from https://app.pulumi.com/account/tokens
    or hit <ENTER> to log in using your browser:
```
To automatically generate and use a new access token, hit `<ENTER>`. This opens a web browser to interact with Pulumi Cloud and request a token. If this is your first time using Pulumi Cloud, you are asked to authenticate using your chosen identity provider (GitHub, GitLab, Atlassian, SAML/SSO, or email).
To view your access tokens, or create a new one manually, view the [Access Tokens](https://app.pulumi.com/account/tokens) page. The page lists past tokens, when they were last used, and lets you revoke them.
To log into a self-hosted instance of Pulumi Cloud, pass its API URL to the `login` command:
```sh
$ pulumi login https://pulumi.acmecorp.com
```
Everything works the same as with the standard Pulumi Cloud, except that Pulumi targets your private instance instead of the shared one hosted at `app.pulumi.com`.
To learn how the Pulumi Cloud backend is designed—including why it never needs your cloud credentials—see [Pulumi Cloud architecture](/docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/#pulumi-cloud-architecture). If you are interested in hosting your own instance, see [Self-Hosted Pulumi Cloud](/docs/administration/self-hosting/).
## Using a DIY backend
You can manage state yourself with a DIY backend that stores state in AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, an S3-compatible server, a PostgreSQL database, or your local filesystem. For setup instructions and per-backend configuration details, see [Using a DIY backend](/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/).
## Refreshing state
Pulumi's state records what your infrastructure looked like after the last `pulumi up` or `pulumi refresh`. When you run `pulumi preview` or `pulumi up`, Pulumi compares this recorded state against the configuration declared in your program to determine which changes need to be made. It does not query each resource directly from your cloud provider on every run.
This means that if someone modifies a resource _outside_ of Pulumi (by editing it in the cloud provider's console, applying a change with a provider CLI, or by some other out-of-band means), that change is not automatically reflected in Pulumi's state. The next `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview` will not account for those changes, and may produce unexpected results including overwriting them.
### Why Pulumi does not refresh automatically
Pulumi intentionally does not refresh state before every operation, for several reasons:
- **Performance**: Querying every resource's live state from the cloud provider can be slow, particularly for large stacks with hundreds or thousands of resources. Doing this implicitly on every `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview` would add significant latency for the typical case where no out-of-band changes have been made.
- **Explicit control**: Pulumi treats your program as the source of truth for desired state. Automatically reconciling out-of-band changes before each operation could cause your program and your actual infrastructure to diverge silently, or could cause Pulumi to preserve changes you intended to overwrite.
- **Predictability**: Keeping refresh explicit means you decide when and whether to incorporate external changes versus overwrite them, giving you confidence about what each `pulumi up` will do.
### Running `pulumi refresh`
To synchronize Pulumi's recorded state with the actual state of your cloud resources, run:
This command queries each resource in your stack from the cloud provider and updates Pulumi's state file to reflect any differences. If a resource has been deleted outside of Pulumi, Pulumi removes it from the state. If properties have changed, Pulumi updates the state to match.
`pulumi refresh` updates only the state. It does not modify your Pulumi program or apply any changes to your infrastructure. If you want to preserve external changes going forward, you also need to update your program to reflect the new configuration; otherwise, the next `pulumi up` will attempt to revert those properties back to what your program declares.
Run `pulumi refresh` when:
- Resources have been modified or deleted outside of Pulumi, such as through the cloud console or another tool.
- You are troubleshooting unexpected diffs during a `pulumi preview` and suspect the state may be stale.
- You want to verify that Pulumi's recorded state accurately reflects reality before running a `pulumi destroy`.
### Refreshing as part of an update
To refresh state and then apply your program's desired state in a single step, pass the `--refresh` flag to `pulumi up`:
Similarly, to preview what an update would look like after first refreshing state:
### Automated drift detection
> This [Pulumi Cloud](/docs/iac/concepts/pulumi-cloud/) feature is available in the [Pro and Enterprise editions](/pricing/#drift-detection).
For teams that want to detect and remediate [out-of-band changes](/what-is/what-is-infrastructure-drift/) on a schedule, Pulumi Cloud provides built-in [drift detection and remediation](/docs/deployments/concepts/drift/). With drift detection configured, Pulumi Cloud periodically runs `pulumi refresh` against your stacks and alerts you (or optionally remediates automatically) when the actual state of your infrastructure diverges from Pulumi's rec
To learn more, see [Drift detection](/docs/deployments/concepts/drift/) for the Pulumi Cloud feature, and [Detecting and reconciling drift](/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/drift/) for the CLI-side workflow (remediation vs. adoption, GitOps continuous reconciliation, and false-positive reduction).
## Advanced state
Pulumi is designed to abstract state management away from you so that you can work with declarative infrastructure as code. In certain advanced cases, you may want or need to interact with state more directly, especially when using DIY backends. In those cases, the following sections may be helpful.
### Importing existing resources
Pulumi supports importing resources that were already created outside of Pulumi, such as resources created using the cloud console, a cloud CLI or SDK, or even another infrastructure as code tool. Resource metadata is imported into your Pulumi state and source code is generated in your chosen language to match that state.
To learn more about importing existing resources, see [Importing Infrastructure](/docs/iac/guides/migration/import/).
### Checkpoints
Pulumi state is usually stored in a transactional snapshot called a _checkpoint_. Pulumi records checkpoints early and often as it executes so that Pulumi can operate reliably, the way database transactions do. The basic functions of state allow Pulumi to diff your program's goal state against the last known update, recover from failure, and destroy resources accurately to clean up afterwards. The checkpoint format augments this with additional f
The Pulumi Cloud backend records every checkpoint through a transactional API, making it possible to transparently recover from unusual failure scenarios such as network interruptions during updates. DIY backends also maintain checkpoint history (in the `.pulumi/history/` directory), but because they are fundamentally limited by the non-transactional protocols of blob storage, they cannot transparently recover from certain kinds of partial failur
### State encryption
State is stored in your target backend in the form of checkpoints. With the Pulumi Cloud backend, all remote communication is done over TLS and data is encrypted at rest.
### Secrets
A Pulumi "secret" can be used to store sensitive configuration values like database passwords and cloud tokens, and will always be handled safely. Pulumi understands the transitive usage of that secret in your state and will ensure everything it touches is encrypted, no matter which backend you've chosen.
A secret can be created one of two ways: passing `--secret` to the `pulumi config set` command, or by [creating one programmatically](/docs/iac/concepts/secrets/#secrets). In both cases, the value is encrypted using your stack's chosen encryption provider. By default with Pulumi Cloud, a server-side HSM key is used, but you may customize the encryption provider if you'd like more control over keys, rotation, and so on.
To learn more about available encryption providers and how to customize your stack's, see [Configuring Secrets Encryption](/docs/iac/concepts/secrets/#configuring-secrets-encryption).

---
title: Policy as code
url: /docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/
---
Policy as code lets you write the rules your infrastructure must follow as code, then check every resource against them automatically. Pulumi Policies applies policy as code to resources you deploy with Pulumi IaC and to resources that Discovery finds in your cloud accounts, however those resources were created.
## What is policy as code?
Policy as code applies software engineering practices to infrastructure rules. Instead of documenting compliance requirements in a wiki or configuring them by hand in each cloud provider's console, you write them as code. content.content:
The open source Pulumi CLI runs policy packs locally. Pass the `--policy-pack` flag to `pulumi preview` or `pulumi up`:
```bash
pulumi preview --policy-pack /path/to/policy-pack
```
To apply more than one policy pack, repeat the flag:
```bash
pulumi up --policy-pack /path/to/pack-1 --policy-pack /path/to/pack-2
```
Local execution works with any backend, including the self-managed backend, and with both open source and custom policy packs. The policy pack must be on disk where you run Pulumi, and the machine needs the pack's [runtime](/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/policy-packs/#runtime-requirements) installed.
#### Pulumi Cloud
> This [Pulumi Cloud](/docs/iac/concepts/pulumi-cloud/) feature is available in the [Essentials, Pro, and Enterprise editions](/pricing/#policy-enforcement).
Pulumi Cloud adds central management on top of local execution:
- Apply policy packs to many stacks and cloud accounts with [policy groups](/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/policy-groups/), without passing `--policy-pack` on each command. Pulumi downloads the packs automatically.
- Use Pulumi's [pre-built policy packs](/docs/discovery-governance/guides/pre-built-policy-packs/): Pulumi Best Practices on the Essentials edition and above, and compliance-framework packs on the Enterprise edition.
- Publish your own packs to your organization, with versioning and rollback.
- Run audit policies against discovered resources. Audit policies require Pulumi Cloud and aren't available with a self-managed backend.
- Track violations across your organization in [Policy Findings](/docs/discovery-governance/operations/policy-findings/).

1. If your team already has a preferred cloud encryption provider that you would like to use.
In both cases, you can continue using secrets management as described above, but instruct Pulumi to use an alternative encryption provider.
### Initializing a stack with alternative encryption
To specify an alternative encryption provider, specify it at stack initialization time:
```
$ pulumi stack init <name> --secrets-provider="<provider>://<provider-settings>"
```
After doing so, all encryption operations for your stack use the custom provider settings. The `<provider>` and `<provider-settings>` are specific to your chosen encryption provider. See [Available encryption providers](#available-encryption-providers) for the supported providers and their options.
Pulumi uses the Go Cloud Development Kit to implement pluggable secrets providers. In the event configuration or authentication options below do not work, the [Go CDK documentation](https://gocloud.dev/howto/secrets/) can be consulted for debugging information.
### Available encryption providers
Pulumi supports the following encryption providers:
- `awskms`: [AWS Key Management Service (KMS)](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/)
- `azurekeyvault`: [Azure Key Vault](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/key-vault/)
- `gcpkms`: [Google Cloud Key Management Service (KMS)](https://cloud.google.com/kms/)

cat >> work/02-research.md <<'EOF' --- ## Topic 4 — Pulumi and Serverless Framework in CI Accessed 2026-11-08. Sources and how they were read (all **local check**, HTTP 200): - **Pulumi docs:** the raw Markdown that pulumi.com serves at `/index.md`. Links point to the canonical URL each page declares. - **Serverless Framework v4 docs:** read from the official repository `serverless/serverless` (`docs/sf/…` on `main`), plus its GitHub release notes. Links point to the docs site. - **AWS CloudFormation pages:** raw `.md` from docs.aws.amazon.com. **Papaya facts that are unknown:** whether Pulumi uses Pulumi Cloud or a DIY (S3) backend, and which Pulumi Cloud edition. The same goes for the Serverless Framework major version and subscription. Each row says when it depends on one of these. ### 4.1 Pulumi: preview and up in CI | # | Finding | Marker | Source | |---|---|---|---| | 4.1.1 | `pulumi preview` flags relevant to CI: `--diff`, `--json`, `--expect-no-changes` ("Return an error if any changes are proposed"), `--policy-pack`, `--refresh`, `--target`, and `--save-plan` (marked **[PREVIEW]**). `--show-secrets` defaults to false; "if used with `--save-plan` the secrets will also be shown in the plan file". | ✅ | [pulumi preview](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_preview/) | | 4.1.2 | `pulumi up` flags: `--yes` ("Automatically approve and perform the update after previewing it"), `--skip-preview`, `--plan ` (**[EXPERIMENTAL]**: "will not perform operations that exceed its plan"), `--strict` (**[EXPERIMENTAL]**: generate a plan during preview and constrain the update to it), and `--expect-no-changes`, where "This check happens after the update is applied". | ✅ | [pulumi up](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_up/) | | 4.1.3 | **Update plans:** "`pulumi preview --save-plan=plan.json`" then "`pulumi up --plan=plan.json`" constrains the update "to allow only the changes described in the plan". The docs say this "may be useful in organizations with strict approval processes".
Limits:
- Values unknown at preview time are recorded as `unknown`.
- Resources created inside an `apply` are not recorded, which causes an error at update time.
- Providers with unknown inputs are not fully diffed.
- The docs say the plan is "not as strong a guarantee as to what the program will do".
- The plan file format "is currently experimental and subject to change". | ✅ | [Update plans](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/update-plans/) | | 4.1.4 | Pulumi's GitHub Actions guide uses `pulumi/actions` (`command: preview` on `pull_request`, `up` on push), with optional PR comments. It recommends **OIDC token exchange** through `pulumi/auth-actions` ("no stored secret") over a stored `PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Cloud credentials come either from Pulumi ESC or directly from cloud OIDC, for example `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials`. The guide assumes Pulumi Cloud, but "Pulumi Cloud isn't required to run Pulumi in CI/CD". | ✅ | [GitHub Actions](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/using-pulumi/continuous-delivery/github-actions/) | | 4.1.5 | **Pulumi Cloud OIDC trust for GitHub:**
- Organization tokens are available on the Essentials, Pro and Enterprise editions; team and personal tokens also exist.
- The example subject is `repo:/:*`. That is the old `sub` format with a wildcard, which matches any branch, PR or environment.
- Setting it up requires being "an admin of your Pulumi organization". | ✅ | [OIDC: GitHub](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/pulumi-cloud/access-management/oidc/client/github/) | ### 4.2 Pulumi: policy as code ("CrossGuard") | # | Finding | Marker | Source | |---|---|---|---| | 4.2.1 | **Naming:** the current docs call the product **"Pulumi Policies"**. "CrossGuard" does not appear in any Pulumi page downloaded (`grep -c -i crossguard` = 0, **local check**). I assume this is the same product renamed (⚠️). | ✅ (name) / ⚠️ (rename) | [Policy as code](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/) | | 4.2.2 | Policies are written in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python or OPA Rego. They run as analyzer plugins during `pulumi preview` and `pulumi up`, "before anything changes in your cloud provider", and "a violation of a mandatory policy stops the deployment". The enforcement levels are `advisory`, `mandatory`, `remediate` and `disabled`. | ✅ | [Policy as code](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/), [Policy packs](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/policy-packs/) | | 4.2.3 | **Two ways to enforce:**
- **Open source, local:** the job runs `--policy-pack `. This works "with any backend, including the self-managed backend". The pack must be on disk where Pulumi runs.
- **Pulumi Cloud** (Essentials, Pro and Enterprise): policy groups apply packs to stacks "without passing `--policy-pack` on each command", and the CLI downloads them automatically. Pre-built compliance packs (CIS, HITRUST, ISO 27001, NIST, PCI DSS) are on Enterprise. Audit policies over discovered resources need Pulumi Cloud. | ✅ | [Policy as code](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/) | | 4.2.4 | **Inference:** with local enforcement, the policy flag lives in the CI workflow. A PR that edits the workflow can drop it, so it is only as strong as CODEOWNERS on `.github/` (3.2.8). Enforcement through Cloud policy groups does not depend on the flag. Whether a CLI user can opt out of Cloud-enforced packs was not found in the pages read (⚠️). | ⚠️ inference | — | ### 4.3 Pulumi: drift, state and secrets | # | Finding | Marker | Source | |---|---|---|---| | 4.3.1 | Pulumi does **not** refresh automatically: preview and up compare the program with the **recorded** state. Out-of-band changes are not seen, and "may produce unexpected results including overwriting them". `pulumi refresh` updates only state. `--refresh` on preview or up refreshes first. | ✅ | [State and backends](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/) | | 4.3.2 | **Drift detection:**
- **Scheduled (Pulumi Cloud Deployments):** available on the **Pro and Enterprise** editions. It runs a refresh periodically and alerts, or optionally remediates.
- **From the CLI:** "`pulumi refresh --preview-only`", which a job on any backend can run on a schedule (inference). | ✅ | [Drift detection and remediation](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/deployments/concepts/drift/), [State and backends](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/) | | 4.3.3 | **Backends:** Pulumi Cloud, the default, or **DIY**: S3, Azure Blob, GCS, an S3-compatible store, PostgreSQL or local disk. "DIY backends include built-in state locking and history tracking". The S3 backend needs `s3:ListBucket`, `GetObject`, `PutObject` and `DeleteObject` under `.pulumi/` "across the full stack lifecycle", including `pulumi preview`. DIY backends "cannot transparently recover from certain kinds of partial failures". | ✅ | [State and backends](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/), [Using a DIY backend](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/) | | 4.3.4 | **Secrets:** Pulumi tracks secrets transitively and encrypts them in state "no matter which backend you've chosen". With Pulumi Cloud the default key is a per-stack key managed by Pulumi Cloud. Alternatives are set with `--secrets-provider` at stack init: `awskms`, `azurekeyvault`, `gcpkms`, `hashivault`, `passphrase`. Config values are plain text unless set with `--secret`. | ✅ | [Secrets](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/secrets/), [State and backends](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/) | | 4.3.5 | **Pulumi Cloud audit logs:** Pro and Enterprise editions. Automatic export to S3 or Microsoft Sentinel: Enterprise only. | ✅ | [Audit logs](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/administration/concepts/audit-logs/) | ### 4.4 Serverless Framework (v4) in CI | # | Finding | Marker | Source | |---|---|---|---| | 4.4.1 | `serverless deploy` turns `serverless.yml` into **one CloudFormation stack** and updates it. Since v4 the default `deploymentMethod` is `direct`, and `changesets` is opt-in. **State is the CloudFormation stack plus the deployment bucket.** Compose services also keep state in S3, located through an SSM parameter in `us-east-1`. | ✅ | [Deploying](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/deploying), [serverless.yml reference](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/serverless.yml), [State](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/state) | | 4.4.2 | **Preview:** `serverless diff` shows Lambda code changes and a structured CloudFormation template diff (resources, **IAM statements**, security groups, outputs), with "(requires replacement)" markers, `--json` "for CI consumption", and `--package` to diff an already built package. It was **added in sf-core 4.37.0 (2026-05-27)**, per the release notes; older v4 versions do not have it. | ✅ | [diff](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/cli-reference/diff), [release sf-core@4.37.0](https://github.com/serverless/serverless/releases/tag/sf-core%404.37.0) | | 4.4.3 | **Build once, deploy that artifact:** `serverless package` then `serverless deploy --package `, which "bypasses the package step and uses the existing package". | ✅ | [Deploying](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/deploying) | | 4.4.4 | **`serverless deploy function`** "does not touch your AWS CloudFormation Stack. Instead, it simply overwrites the zip file of the current function". The docs present it as a fast development path. | ✅ | [Deploying](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/deploying) | | 4.4.5 | `provider.iam.deploymentRole`: "ARN of an IAM role for CloudFormation service. If specified, CloudFormation uses the role's credentials". AWS warns: "It is not possible to remove a service role attached to a stack after the stack is created". Also: "Other users that have permissions to perform operations on this stack are able to use this role, regardless of whether those users have the `iam:PassRole` permission". Other relevant options: `stackPolicy`, `rollbackConfiguration`, `disableRollback` (non-prod). | ✅ | [serverless.yml reference](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/serverless.yml), [CloudFormation service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-iam-servicerole.html) | | 4.4.6 | **Drift:** Serverless has no drift command. `serverless reconcile` is about billing ("reconciles your org's list of billable instances"). CloudFormation drift detection applies to the stack, with limits: it covers only resource types that support it (others are `NOT_CHECKED`), and only "property values that are explicitly set", not defaults. | ✅ | [reconcile](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/cli-reference/reconcile), [CloudFormation drift detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-stack-drift.html) | | 4.4.7 | **Secrets:** `${ssm:…}` variables, and Secrets Manager through `ssm:/aws/reference/secretsmanager/…`. They are resolved with "the deployment (provider) AWS credentials". SecureString values are decrypted unless `noDecrypt` is set. Whether resolved values then sit in plain text in the CloudFormation template, for example as Lambda environment variables, is not stated on the page read (⚠️). | ✅ / ⚠️ | [Variables: SSM & Secrets Manager](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/variables/aws/ssm) | | 4.4.8 | **Licensing and authentication:** "Starting with Version 4, authentication is required for all users". Organizations with "annual revenue exceeding $2M USD" need a subscription. In CI, **License Keys** "do not offer access control or permissions", have "No Expiration" (rotate them as a best practice), and disable Dashboard access. | ✅ | [License keys](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/license-keys), [Upgrading to v4](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/upgrading-v4) | ### 4.5 Mapping to Terraform / OpenTofu (one sentence) In Terraform/OpenTofu terms: - `pulumi preview` ≈ `plan`; - `pulumi up` ≈ `apply`; - an update plan ≈ applying a saved plan file; - `pulumi refresh` ≈ a refresh-only plan; - Pulumi Policies ≈ Sentinel/OPA; - Pulumi Cloud or a DIY S3 backend ≈ HCP Terraform or an S3 backend. So the controls below carry over to Terraform/OpenTofu shops. Marker: 📖 for the Pulumi side and the existence of Sentinel ([Pulumi vs Terraform](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/comparisons/terraform/)); ⚠️ for the exact Terraform/OpenTofu command names, whose docs were not read this session. ### 4.6 What this means for Papaya (inferences — to be used in the design) These are my conclusions from the findings above, not documented facts: 1. **Make "what the reviewer approved" equal "what gets applied".** - **Pulumi:** run `pulumi preview --diff` with policies on the PR, and post it as a PR comment for the reviewer. On merge, run `pulumi up` from `main` under the `production` environment (3.6 #1). - **Option, `--save-plan` / `up --plan`:** it ties the apply to the reviewed preview, but it is preview/experimental and has documented gaps (4.1.3). Treat it as a guard, not as proof. Plan files can carry secrets if `--show-secrets` is used (4.1.1). - **Serverless:** `sls diff --json` on the PR (requires ≥ 4.37.0, 4.4.2); on merge, `package` then `deploy --package` of the same artifact (4.4.3). 2. **A PR preview needs prod read access, and runs the PR's code.** - `pulumi preview` executes the program, and with an S3 backend it also writes lock objects (4.3.3). `sls diff` packages the service and reads the deployed stack (4.4.2). - So a PR job that previews prod needs a **separate read-only "plan" role**. That role must still be treated as exposed to PR code: anyone who can open a PR can run code with it. - Under GĐ-9 / 1.11, the plan role must not have data-plane reads on PHI stores. - The apply role exists only for `main` + `production`. - This is a tension with 3.6 #1 ("only `main` gets prod credentials"). It is resolved by having two roles with different trust: a `pr-preview` environment or `pull_request` sub for the plan role, and `environment:production` for the apply role. 3. **Close the bypass paths in the tools themselves:** - `serverless deploy function` skips CloudFormation and its review (4.4.4). Deny it in prod via IAM (`lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` only for the CloudFormation deployment role, 4.4.5, ⚠️ design). - Use a least-privilege `deploymentRole`. It cannot be removed later, and anyone who may operate the stack can use it (4.4.5). - Pulumi `--target` and `--skip-preview` should not appear in prod workflows (4.1.1, 4.1.2). 4. **Policy as code where the agent can't switch it off.** - Prefer Pulumi Cloud policy groups (Essentials+) if Papaya is on Pulumi Cloud. - Otherwise use `--policy-pack` in a CODEOWNERS-protected reusable workflow (4.2.3, 4.2.4). - For Serverless, the CloudFormation template from `sls package` can be checked by a CI policy tool (⚠️ tool not researched). Plus IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on changed policies (2.8.1). 5. **Drift is a compliance signal, because it means an unreviewed change happened.** - **Pulumi:** scheduled `pulumi refresh --preview-only` or `preview --expect-no-changes` in CI (any backend), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection (Pro+) (4.3.2). - **Serverless:** scheduled CloudFormation drift detection, with its coverage limits (4.4.6). - Every drift finding should map to a CloudTrail actor (2.5) and an incident or ticket. 6. **State and secrets:** - Pulumi state and Serverless state buckets are **prod-sensitive stores**. They hold encrypted secrets and resource details. Restrict them to the deploy roles (4.3.3, 4.4.1). - Use a cloud-KMS secrets provider (`awskms`) if Papaya uses a DIY backend (4.3.4). - Serverless secrets should be resolved at runtime, not baked into templates (⚠️ 4.4.7). - The Serverless License Key is a long-lived CI secret with no access control (4.4.8). Keep it in the environment, not repository secrets (3.5.3b). ### 4.7 Open items (Topic 4) - [ ] ⚠️ Papaya's Pulumi backend (Pulumi Cloud vs DIY S3) and edition; Serverless version (≥ 4.37.0 for `diff`?) and subscription. - [ ] ⚠️ Can a CLI user bypass Pulumi Cloud policy-group enforcement (4.2.4)? - [ ] ⚠️ Do Serverless-resolved SSM/Secrets Manager values end up in plain text in the CloudFormation template (4.4.7)? - [ ] ⚠️ The exact Terraform/OpenTofu command names (4.5); CI policy tools for CloudFormation templates (4.6 #4). ### 4.8 Review log (Topic 4) (to be filled after the independent review) EOF grep -c '' work/02-research.md

It cannot be removed later, and anyone who may operate the stack can use it (4.4.5). - Pulumi `--target` and `--skip-preview` should not appear in prod workflows (4.1.1, 4.1.2). 4. **Policy as code where the agent can't switch it off.** - Prefer Pulumi Cloud policy groups (Essentials+) if Papaya is on Pulumi Cloud. - Otherwise use `--policy-pack` in a CODEOWNERS-protected reusable workflow (4.2.3, 4.2.4). - For Serverless, the CloudFormation template from `sls package` can be checked by a CI policy tool (⚠️ tool not researched). Plus IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on changed policies (2.8.1). 5. **Drift is a compliance signal, because it means an unreviewed change happened.** - **Pulumi:** scheduled `pulumi refresh --preview-only` or `preview --expect-no-changes` in CI (any backend), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection (Pro+) (4.3.2). - **Serverless:** scheduled CloudFormation drift detection, with its coverage limits (4.4.6). - Every drift finding should map to a CloudTrail actor (2.5) and an incident or ticket. 6. **State and secrets:** - Pulumi state and Serverless state buckets are **prod-sensitive stores**. +   - **Pulumi:** run `pulumi preview --diff` with policies on the PR, and post it as a PR comment
+     for the reviewer. On merge, run `pulumi up` from `main` under the `production` environment
+   - **Option, `--save-plan` / `up --plan`:** it ties the apply to the reviewed preview, but it is
+     preview/experimental and has documented gaps (4.1.3). Treat it as a guard, not as proof.
+     Plan files can carry secrets if `--show-secrets` is used (4.1.1).
+   - **Serverless:** `sls diff --json` on the PR (requires ≥ 4.37.0, 4.4.2); on merge,
+     `package` then `deploy --package` of the same artifact (4.4.3).
+2. **A PR preview needs prod read access, and runs the PR's code.**
+   - `pulumi preview` executes the program, and with an S3 backend it also writes lock objects
+     (4.3.3). `sls diff` packages the service and reads the deployed stack (4.4.2).
+   - So a PR job that previews prod needs a **separate read-only "plan" role**. That role must
+     still be treated as exposed to PR code: anyone who can open a PR can run code with it.
+   - Under GĐ-9 / 1.11, the plan role must not have data-plane reads on PHI stores.
+   - The apply role exists only for `main` + `production`.
+   - This is a tension with 3.6 #1 ("only `main` gets prod credentials"). It is resolved by having
+     two roles with different trust: a `pr-preview` environment or `pull_request` sub for the plan
+     role, and `environment:production` for the apply role.
+3. **Close the bypass paths in the tools themselves:**
+   - `serverless deploy function` skips CloudFormation and its review (4.4.4). Deny it in prod via
+     IAM (`lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` only for the CloudFormation deployment role, 4.4.5, ⚠️
+     design).
+   - Use a least-privilege `deploymentRole`. It cannot be removed later, and anyone who may
+     operate the stack can use it (4.4.5).
+   - Pulumi `--target` and `--skip-preview` should not appear in prod workflows (4.1.1, 4.1.2).
+4. **Policy as code where the agent can't switch it off.**
+   - Prefer Pulumi Cloud policy groups (Essentials+) if Papaya is on Pulumi Cloud.
+   - Otherwise use `--policy-pack` in a CODEOWNERS-protected reusable workflow (4.2.3, 4.2.4).
+   - For Serverless, the CloudFormation template from `sls package` can be checked by a CI policy
+     tool (⚠️ tool not researched). Plus IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on changed
+     policies (2.8.1).
+5. **Drift is a compliance signal, because it means an unreviewed change happened.**
+   - **Pulumi:** scheduled `pulumi refresh --preview-only` or `preview --expect-no-changes` in CI
+     (any backend), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection (Pro+) (4.3.2).
+   - **Serverless:** scheduled CloudFormation drift detection, with its coverage limits (4.4.6).
+   - Every drift finding should map to a CloudTrail actor (2.5) and an incident or ticket.
+6. **State and secrets:**
+   - Pulumi state and Serverless state buckets are **prod-sensitive stores**. They hold encrypted
+     secrets and resource details. Restrict them to the deploy roles (4.3.3, 4.4.1).
+   - Use a cloud-KMS secrets provider (`awskms`) if Papaya uses a DIY backend (4.3.4).
+   - Serverless secrets should be resolved at runtime, not baked into templates (⚠️ 4.4.7).
+   - The Serverless License Key is a long-lived CI secret with no access control (4.4.8). Keep it
+     in the environment, not repository secrets (3.5.3b).
+### 4.7 Open items (Topic 4)
+- [ ] ⚠️ Papaya's Pulumi backend (Pulumi Cloud vs DIY S3) and edition; Serverless version
+      (≥ 4.37.0 for `diff`?) and subscription.
+- [ ] ⚠️ Can a CLI user bypass Pulumi Cloud policy-group enforcement (4.2.4)?
+- [ ] ⚠️ Do Serverless-resolved SSM/Secrets Manager values end up in plain text in the
+      CloudFormation template (4.4.7)?
+- [ ] ⚠️ The exact Terraform/OpenTofu command names (4.5); CI policy tools for CloudFormation
+      templates (4.6 #4).

- Hệ quả 2: thay đổi này tồn tại lâu dài và deploy CloudFormation tiếp theo không sửa lại được.
- Hệ quả 3: biện pháp "chỉ CFN deployment role được UpdateFunctionCode" chỉ có tác dụng khi đã đặt `deploymentRole`. Nếu không đặt, CFN dùng credentials của người gọi, tức chính CI role cũng gọi được `deploy function`.
- Fix: cite thêm trang `cli-reference/deploy-function`, sửa #3 theo ba hệ quả trên. Có thể nêu `aws:CalledVia` là phương án, gắn ⚠️.

### MEDIUM

**M1. 4.6 #5: `preview --expect-no-changes` không phát hiện drift.**
- Preview so program với state đã ghi và "does not query each resource" (state-and-backends:137–139).
- Fix: phải dùng `preview --refresh --expect-no-changes`, hoặc `refresh --preview-only`. Trang drift còn trỏ tới `/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/drift/` ("`--expect-no-changes` for CI"), trang này chưa đọc.

**M2. 4.3.2 nói "optionally remediates" nhưng không cảnh báo xung đột compliance.**
- Auto-remediation "runs `pulumi up --refresh`" (drift.md:40). Đây là thay đổi prod không có người duyệt, trái yêu cầu Compliance.
- Fix: ghi rõ phải tắt auto-remediate trên prod. Ngoài ra, drift qua Deployments cần "deployment settings" (drift.md:11), tức Pulumi Cloud giữ credentials prod.

**M3. 4.6 #1: preview có thể cũ so với lúc apply.**
- Với Team plan, không có merge queue (3.7), preview trên PR được tính so với base tại thời điểm PR. Sau khi PR khác merge, `up` trên `main` có thể khác cái người review đã thấy.
- Fix: ruleset bật "require branches up to date" (status check strict), hoặc chạy preview lại trên `main` rồi so sánh.
- Đi kèm: concurrency group cho deploy không bật `cancel-in-progress`. Guide GitHub Actions của Pulumi khuyến nghị đúng điều này (github-actions.md:640–655, "canceling a deployment mid-run can leave infrastructure half-applied"); hiện chưa được ghi lại.

**M4. 4.6 #3: danh sách flag hoặc lệnh bypass chưa đủ.**
- Flag còn thiếu: `--exclude`, `--target-replace`, `--replace` (đều có trong preview/up).
- Lệnh thay đổi state không qua review: `pulumi state …`, `import`, `destroy`, `stack rm`.
- Fix: dùng allowlist lệnh trong reusable workflow thay vì denylist.

**M5. 4.6 #2 nói "giải quyết" tension với 3.6 nhưng chưa xét các trường hợp sau.**
- (a) `sub` của PR là `repo:<org>/<repo>:pull_request`, ai có quyền write đều mở PR được. Trên Team, environment `pr-preview` không có gate.
- (b) Job drift theo lịch (#5) cần trust thứ ba (`ref:refs/heads/main` hoặc một environment riêng), trong khi 3.6 #2 chỉ trust `environment:production`.
- Fix: liệt kê đủ các role, trust và mục đích tương ứng.

**M6. 4.2.1: đổi tên CrossGuard có bằng chứng, nên nâng từ ⚠️ lên ✅.**
- `curl -sIL https://www.pulumi.com/docs/using-pulumi/crossguard/` redirect (200) tới `/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/`.
- `/docs/iac/using-pulumi/crossguard/` cũng redirect về cùng trang đó.
- README của `pulumi/pulumi-policy` vẫn link "Policy as Code" tới `/docs/guides/crossguard/`.

### LOW

- **L1. Link không canonical**, trái với cam kết ở dòng 910. Cả hai URL vẫn redirect (200), nhưng front matter khai báo URL khác:
  - 4.1.4 nên là `/docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/github-actions/`.
  - 4.1.5 nên là `/docs/administration/guides/oidc-issuers/github/`.
- **L2. 4.3.2 cite sai nguồn.** `refresh --preview-only` không có trong trang State and backends; nó nằm ở trang `pulumi_refresh` CLI (dòng 45) và trang drift (dòng 15).
- **L3. 4.5 dùng marker 📖 cho trang Pulumi vs Terraform**, nhưng file đã được tải và đọc (`docs_iac_comparisons_terraform.md`, Sentinel ở dòng 102), nên phải là ✅.
  - Tiêu đề ghi "one sentence" nhưng nội dung là danh sách.
  - Mục "update plan ≈ saved plan" so sánh quá đà: tài liệu Pulumi tự nói plan "not as strong a guarantee".
- **L4. 4.4.2 thiếu chi tiết quan trọng cho CI.** `sls diff` "exits `0` … Differences … do not cause a non-zero exit code — the command is informational" (cli_diff.md:227). Muốn làm gate thì CI phải tự parse `--json`.
- **L5. 4.6 #2 ghi "preview executes the program" mà không có nguồn**, trong khi có sẵn: preview synopsis "The new desired state is computed by running a Pulumi program". Chi tiết "writes lock objects" khi preview là suy luận, cần gắn nhãn.
- **L6. 4.1.5:**
  - Team token chỉ có trên Pro/Enterprise, chưa ghi.
  - Câu "old `sub` format with wildcard" là suy luận, cần gắn nhãn.
  - Chưa nói policy của Pulumi có pin được `environment:production` hay không (⚠️).
- **L7. 4.6 #6: License Key có phương án tốt hơn.** Có thể lưu trong SSM của từng account, framework đọc bằng deploy credentials (≥ 4.4.19, license-keys.md:150–164). Như vậy không cần GitHub secret nào.
- **L8. 4.2.4: chưa đánh giá đủ ý nghĩa của policy trong PR preview.** Policy pack "run on the machine that runs Pulumi" (policy-packs.md:37), cùng máy với code của PR, nên enforcement chỉ thực sự có hiệu lực ở `up` trên `main`. Ngoài ra `pulumi policy disable` (policy-groups.md:47,74) cho thấy ai có quyền admin Pulumi org thì tắt được policy. Cần đưa vào câu hỏi mở 4.7.
- **L9. Enforcement level `remediate`** "fixes the resource automatically": tài nguyên có thể khác với code người review đã đọc. Cần ghi chú.

### Coverage gaps (theo scope owner yêu cầu)

1. **Các đường SaaS bên thứ ba cấp credentials prod, không đi qua gate GitHub environment:**
   - Pulumi ESC (guide gọi đây là "the recommended way to provide cloud credentials", github-actions.md:52);
   - Pulumi Deployments (Click to Deploy, schedules, `--remote`);
   - Serverless Dashboard Providers / `provider.resolver` (credentials.md:111–264).
   
   Mỗi đường là một trust path tới AWS prod cần được xử lý: cấm dùng, hoặc đặt dưới cùng gate. Đây là gap lớn nhất.
2. **Pulumi Cloud RBAC/teams và stack tags:** ai được sửa policy group, ai giữ org token.
3. **Resource options `protect`, `retainOnDelete`, `ignoreChanges`:** chưa có trong tài liệu, trong khi `ignoreChanges` che drift (kit rule §4).
4. **CloudFormation:**
   - change set (`deploymentMethod: changesets`) dùng làm artifact để review: file `cfn_using-cfn-updating-stacks-changesets.md` đã tải nhưng chưa dùng;
   - stack termination protection;
   - `stackPolicy` đã có nhưng chưa được đưa vào 4.6.
5. **Serverless secrets:** `.env`/`.env.${stage}` được nạp tự động thành `${env:}` (slsyml.md:98), `licenseKey` lấy qua resolver, flag `--aws-profile` trên `diff` và `deploy function`.
6. **Bổ sung vào 4.7 Open items:**
   - drift CFN có bắt được thay đổi do `deploy function` gây ra không (Lambda `Code` không phải property tự set rõ ràng nên có thể không bị kiểm tra, ⚠️);
   - trang `/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/drift/` chưa đọc;
   - các mục H1, H2 và M3.

**Tổng: HIGH 2 · MEDIUM 6 · LOW 9 · coverage gap 6.**

### 4.5 Mapping to Terraform / OpenTofu
These are my conclusions from the findings above, not documented facts:
1. **Make "what the reviewer approved" equal "what gets applied", as far as the tools allow.**
-   - **Pulumi:** `pulumi preview --diff` with policies on the PR, posted as a PR comment. On
-     merge, `pulumi up` from `main` under the `production` environment (3.6 #1).
-     `--save-plan` / `up --plan` is a guard, not proof (preview/experimental, documented gaps;
-     4.1.3). Plan files can carry secrets if `--show-secrets` is used (4.1.1).
-   - **Serverless:** `sls diff --json` on the PR, parsed by CI because it always exits 0 (4.4.2).
-     On merge, `package` then `deploy --package` of the same artifact (4.4.3).
-   - **Staleness:** a PR preview is computed against the base at that time. Other merges can change
-     what `up` does (no merge queue, 3.7).
-     - Require branches to be up to date (strict status checks), **or** re-run the preview on
-       `main` and stop if it differs from the reviewed one (⚠️ design).
-     - Deploy jobs share a concurrency group **without** `cancel-in-progress` (4.1.4).
+   - **What the PR reviewer sees:** after #2, a PR shows only **non-prod** previews (`pulumi
+     preview --diff` with policies, `sls diff --json` parsed by CI because it always exits 0,
+     4.4.2). The prod diff differs, because prod has different stack config and state.
+   - **On merge:** `pulumi up` / `package` + `deploy --package` from `main` under `production`
+     (3.6 #1, 4.4.3). Deploy jobs share a concurrency group **without** `cancel-in-progress`
+   - **Core tension on Team:** with the assumed Team plan (3.7 A1), the merge is the approval for
+     prod, yet **no human sees the prod diff before it is applied**. This should be stated
+     openly to the panel. Options (all ⚠️ design):
+     - (a) **Enterprise:** a prod preview job, then the environment approval, then `up`. The
+       approver sees the prod diff (3.1.1).
+     - (b) **Team:** the deploy workflow on `main` previews prod and **stops automatically** on
+       risky changes: replace or delete of stateful resources, IAM changes, policy violations.
+       Those cases need a second, separate approval path. Safe diffs proceed. This uses
+       `--save-plan` / `up --plan` as a guard only (4.1.3).
+     - (c) A prod-preview identity that cannot write state, for example a Pulumi Cloud stack-read
+       token. Its preview could then be shown on the PR. Unverified whether preview works with
+       read-only access (4.7).
+   - **Staleness:** a PR preview is computed against the base at that time (no merge queue, 3.7).
+     Require branches to be up to date (strict status checks).
+   - **Plan files:** `--save-plan` files can carry secrets if `--show-secrets` is used (4.1.1).
2. **PR previews against prod are not read-only, so do not give PRs prod credentials.**
- **State writes:** with an S3 backend, Pulumi needs `PutObject`/`DeleteObject` on `.pulumi/`
"across the full stack lifecycle", including preview (4.3.3). PR code running with that role
- Splitting S3 permissions so that preview can write only `locks/` is ⚠️ unverified. The docs
list permissions for the whole lifecycle, not per command.
- **Roles and trust needed (AWS), each scoped by the `sub` in the repo's format (3.7 A2):**
-     - **non-prod plan/apply:** trusts `pull_request` or non-prod environments;
+     - **non-prod plan/apply:** trusts `pull_request` or non-prod environments. PR code can
+       therefore apply to non-prod, which is acceptable because non-prod holds no real data
- **prod deploy:** trusts `environment:production` only;
- **prod drift check:** a separate read role trusted only from a dedicated `drift`
environment restricted to `main`. It must not be able to change state, so state writes
stay with the deploy role (⚠️ whether refresh preview needs lock writes, see 4.7).
+       It probably needs `kms:Decrypt`, or Pulumi Cloud stack read, to read state that
+       contains secrets. The drift job can then read prod secrets, which must be noted and
+       restricted.
3. **Close the bypass paths inside the tools:**
- **`serverless deploy function`** changes code **and configuration** outside CloudFormation.
The change persists after the next deploy (4.4.4). In prod, deny
the stack can use it (4.4.5). Add a `stackPolicy` for stateful resources.
- **Pulumi:** prod workflows use an **allowlist** of commands and flags (`preview`, `up`
without `--target`, `--target-replace`, `--replace`, `--exclude` or `--skip-preview`).
-     State-changing commands (`state …`, `import`, `destroy`, `stack rm`) are not available
-     through the prod role except in a separately approved run.
+     IAM cannot tell `pulumi` commands apart: the deploy role can write state anyway. So keeping
+     state-changing commands (`state …`, `import`, `destroy`, `stack rm`) out of prod runs is
+     enforced only by the workflow allowlist plus CODEOWNERS on `.github/` (3.2.8). Any other
+     use needs a separately approved run.
4. **Policy as code where the agent can't switch it off.**
- **Enforcement point:** the policy that counts is the one evaluated during `up` on `main`
- [ ] ⚠️ Not covered yet: Pulumi resource options `protect`, `retainOnDelete` and `ignoreChanges`

**Review:**
- **Vòng 1:** 2 HIGH, 6 MEDIUM, 9 LOW, 6 chỗ thiếu.
- **Vòng 2:** còn 1 MEDIUM, 7 LOW.
- **Vòng 3:** còn 1 MEDIUM, 1 LOW.
- **Vòng 4:** sạch.

Mình tự kiểm lại mọi lỗi HIGH/MEDIUM với tài liệu gốc trước khi sửa. Hai lỗi HIGH ở vòng 1:
- Mình gọi role preview cho PR là "read-only". Thực tế nó **ghi được state** (backend S3 cần `PutObject`/`DeleteObject`) và **giải mã được secret prod**, trong khi preview chạy code của PR.
- `serverless deploy function` giờ đổi cả **config** lẫn code, ngoài CloudFormation. Lần `serverless deploy` sau cũng không hoàn tác thay đổi config này.

**Bạn cần biết một điểm (4.6 #1).** Với giả định gói Team, chuyện người duyệt PR thấy diff prod là không làm được an toàn: PR chỉ được preview non-prod, nên lúc merge, **không ai thấy diff prod trước khi nó được áp dụng**. Mình ghi thẳng điểm này cho panel và nêu 3 phương án để xử lý ở bước thiết kế:
- (a) Enterprise: preview prod, rồi environment approval, rồi `up`.
- (b) Team: workflow trên `main` preview prod và **tự dừng** khi gặp thay đổi rủi ro (replace/delete tài nguyên có dữ liệu, đổi IAM, vi phạm policy); trường hợp đó cần một đường duyệt riêng.
- (c) Một identity preview không ghi được state. Phương án này vẫn để code của PR đọc được secret prod, nên chỉ dùng được nếu stack prod không chứa secret.

**Phát hiện chính khác:**
- **Pulumi:**
  - `--save-plan` / `up --plan` ràng buộc lần apply theo preview, nhưng đang ở mức preview/experimental và có giới hạn được ghi trong docs. Chỉ coi là lớp bảo vệ thêm, không phải bằng chứng.
  - "CrossGuard" là tên cũ của **Pulumi Policies**: URL cũ redirect sang trang policy-as-code. Policy chạy local thì PR bỏ được flag; enforcement thật là lúc `up` trên `main`, hoặc qua policy groups trên Pulumi Cloud (gói Essentials trở lên). Admin vẫn tắt được bằng `pulumi policy disable`.
  - Preview không tự refresh, nên muốn bắt drift phải dùng `--refresh` hoặc `refresh --preview-only`. Drift tự động của Pulumi Cloud cần gói Pro trở lên, và chế độ auto-remediate chạy `up` không qua duyệt, nên phải tắt trên prod.
- **Serverless:**
  - `sls diff` mới có từ bản 4.37.0 (27/05/2026) và luôn exit 0, nên CI phải tự parse kết quả JSON.
  - Serverless không có lệnh drift (`reconcile` là lệnh tính phí license). Drift detection của CloudFormation có giới hạn về độ phủ.
  - License key không có quyền hạn gì và không hết hạn. Từ bản 4.4.19 có thể để trong SSM, không cần secret trong GitHub.
- **Đường credential nằm ngoài cổng GitHub:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments và Serverless Dashboard Providers. Mặc định không dùng cho prod; nếu dùng thì phải hẹp như đường `production`.
- **Terraform/OpenTofu:** có một câu ánh xạ thuật ngữ. Tên lệnh phía Terraform đánh ⚠️, vì phiên này chưa đọc docs Terraform.

**Cần hỏi Papaya hoặc kiểm thêm** (mục 4.7):
- Papaya dùng backend Pulumi nào (Pulumi Cloud hay S3) và gói nào? Serverless bản nào?
- Preview có chạy được với quyền chỉ đọc không?
- Secret do Serverless resolve có nằm dạng plain text trong template CloudFormation không?
- Drift detection của CloudFormation có bắt được thay đổi do `deploy function` không?

You help a DevOps/Cloud engineer who works on real infrastructure (Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible, Azure/AWS/GCP, on-prem). A mistake here can break running systems and real data. Safety and proof are more important than speed.

## 2. Read-only first, mutating later

- Read-only: get, describe, logs, top, diff, plan, validate, template, lint, `--check`, `--dry-run`, show/list.
- Mutating: apply, create, delete, patch, replace, scale, rollout restart/undo, exec, install/upgrade/rollback/uninstall, terraform apply/import/state, ansible-playbook without `--check`, `git push` to a GitOps repo, SQL DDL/DML, cloud CLI commands that create/update/delete/set.

- Right before each mutating command, write 4 lines:
  - **What:** …
  - **Target:** the exact context / namespace / resource
  - **Reversible?:** yes / no / partly, and why
  - **Undo:** the exact command, or "not possible, needs backup X"
- Do not add `-auto-approve`, `--yes`, `--force`, `--grace-period=0` unless the user clearly asks for it.

## 3. Risk levels

| Level | Example | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| L0 read-only | debug, read logs, write docs | do it directly |
| L1 dev/sandbox, can be undone | test a component on a dev cluster | short plan → do → verify → change record |
| L2 shared environment, stateless | upgrade Grafana on prod | ask the user to run `/infra-task` |
| L3 stateful / cannot be undone / network / IAM | migrate a DB, change StorageClass, change CIDR, IAM | stop and ask for `/infra-task`; a backup that was test-restored is required |

If you are not sure about the level, choose the higher one and explain why.

## 4. Existing systems (brownfield)

- Follow the conventions that already exist in the repo/cluster, even if they are different from the kit's standards. Write the differences in the **Recommendations** part of your report. Do not fix things outside the task.

Before you plan a change, compare the code with the live state for the parts you touch, and list the ignore rules that cover them. If the project's CLAUDE.md names a source of truth, follow it, but still report the differences.

## 5. Secrets

## Commit Message Format
```
<type>: <description>

<optional body>
```

Types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf, ci

## Pull Request Workflow

When creating PRs:
1. Analyze full commit history (not just latest commit)
2. Use `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to see all changes

# CLAUDE.md — Papaya DevSecOps Challenge 1

## Purpose of this repo

This repository is my submission for Papaya's **DevSecOps Challenge 1 — "DevSecOps with
Coding Agents at Papaya"** (full text: `work/00-challenge.md`). The task is to design the
framework and workflow for how Papaya uses coding agents (Claude Code) for DevSecOps,
reconciling two positions:

- Engineering: "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly."
- Compliance: "Nothing changes in production without a named human who reviewed and approved it."

Two things make this repo unusual and shape every rule below:

1. **The complete, raw Claude Code session transcripts are part of the submission** and are
   graded. Work transparently: state the reason behind each recommendation, show trade-offs,
   and say so when something is unverified.
2. **I have no access to Papaya's systems or code**, and the challenge does not expect it.
   Everything is a design on top of the stack described in the challenge's Appendix A.

## Hard constraints from the brief

- Design for Papaya's existing stack: AWS (Lambda via Serverless Framework, ECS, EC2, Aurora
  PostgreSQL, SNS/SQS, Step Functions, S3, CloudWatch), GCP (Vertex AI, Gemini), k0s
  Kubernetes, Firebase Hosting, a single GitHub monorepo, GitHub Actions, Pulumi, Claude Code
  (Team Premium) with an internal plugin marketplace, Linear, Slack.
- **Do not propose replacing IaC or CI tooling** (no "switch Pulumi to Terraform", no "move off
  GitHub Actions"). Improve how they are used.
- Compliance context: ISO 27001 (in progress), HIPAA, regional data-protection law; multiple
  insurer tenants in different countries. Sensitive data: medical records, national IDs, bank
  accounts.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents | Language |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | Entry point for graders: what the deliverable is, how to read it | English |
| `docs/` | The deliverable: framework, workflows, policies, rollout plan | English |
| `examples/` | Concrete, copy-pasteable artifacts: Claude Code settings/hooks, GitHub Actions workflows, IAM/OIDC policy sketches, plugin manifests | English |
| `diagrams/` | Architecture and workflow diagrams (source + rendered) | English labels |
| `work/` | Working notes, the challenge text (`00-challenge.md`), scratch analysis, decision log | Vietnamese or English |
| `transcripts/` | Copies of the raw Claude Code session files (`*.jsonl`) for this project, unedited | n/a |
| `CLAUDE.md` | This file | English |

Numbered prefixes (`00-`, `01-`, …) in `docs/` and `work/` define reading order. Running logs
that are not part of the reading order stay unnumbered (e.g. `work/session-log.md`).

## Rule 1 — Every claim about a tool's capability needs a source marker

The deliverable depends on what Claude Code, GitHub Actions, AWS IAM, Pulumi, k0s etc. can
actually do. Model memory is often stale. Therefore every non-trivial statement about a
feature, flag, setting, default, or limit carries one of these markers:

| Marker | Meaning | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | Verified in this environment | A command run in this session with its output, or a file read here |
| 📖 | Taken from official documentation | A link to the specific doc page, ideally with the version/date |
| ⚠️ | Assumption or recollection, not verified | Say what would be needed to verify it |

Rules of use:

# Git Workflow

## Commit Message Format
```
<type>: <description>

<optional body>
```

Types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf, ci

Note: ECC-managed installs set `"includeCoAuthoredBy": false` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, so commits carry no `Co-Authored-By` trailer by default. To keep Claude attribution, set `"includeCoAuthoredBy": true` or configure `attribution`; ECC never overwrites an explicit choice.

## Pull Request Workflow

When creating PRs:
1. Analyze full commit history (not just latest commit)
2. Use `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to see all changes
3. Draft comprehensive PR summary
4. Include test plan with TODOs
5. Push with `-u` flag if new branch

> For the full development process (planning, TDD, code review) before git operations,
> see [development-workflow.md](./development-workflow.md).

# CLAUDE.md — Papaya DevSecOps Challenge 1

## Purpose of this repo

This repository is my submission for Papaya's **DevSecOps Challenge 1 — "DevSecOps with
Coding Agents at Papaya"** (full text: `work/00-challenge.md`). The task is to design the
framework and workflow for how Papaya uses coding agents (Claude Code) for DevSecOps,
reconciling two positions:

- Engineering: "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly."
- Compliance: "Nothing changes in production without a named human who reviewed and approved it."

Two things make this repo unusual and shape every rule below:

1. **The complete, raw Claude Code session transcripts are part of the submission** and are
   graded. Work transparently: state the reason behind each recommendation, show trade-offs,
   and say so when something is unverified.
2. **I have no access to Papaya's systems or code**, and the challenge does not expect it.
   Everything is a design on top of the stack described in the challenge's Appendix A.

## Hard constraints from the brief

- Design for Papaya's existing stack: AWS (Lambda via Serverless Framework, ECS, EC2, Aurora
  PostgreSQL, SNS/SQS, Step Functions, S3, CloudWatch), GCP (Vertex AI, Gemini), k0s
  Kubernetes, Firebase Hosting, a single GitHub monorepo, GitHub Actions, Pulumi, Claude Code
  (Team Premium) with an internal plugin marketplace, Linear, Slack.
